# GPS-denied navigation: solution test report

*Test run on 2026-10-23. Branch `claude/new-session-peh13r`, folder `gpsdenied-eval/`. Every number comes from a logged run under `results/`; this document is generated by `harness/report_build.py`.*

## 1. Executive summary

**What was tested.** Six GPS-denied navigation solutions (S1-S6) and three paper-only items (S7) on the same synthetic NIDAR-like video, the same reference map and the same metric code, plus an ArduPilot SITL loop. The real NIDAR video, GPU, Jetson and the fallback datasets (MAFS, MUN-FRL, ALTO) were **not available**, so every result is on synthetic data, on CPU, with a map that is the same imagery the video was rendered from. Accuracy numbers are therefore **optimistic** and the ranking is about relative behaviour, not absolute field accuracy.

**Ranking (owner weights).** 1. S6 our composite (Jetson baseline) (8.29), 2. S5 SWA-PF (7.78), 3. S3 tile-matching (Shuhaieva) (4.53), then S1 koksalan/gnss-denied-nav (4.25), S2 uav-geolocalization (CAEVL + VIO) (2.38), S4 hmakelin/gisnav (0.79). The sensitivity check keeps the same winner under every weight change, so a single overall winner is stated.

| Rank | Solution | Weighted score (0-10) | Accuracy (30%) | Robustness (20%) | Real-time and edge fit (20%) | SITL outcome (15%) | Integration, documentation and licence (15%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | S6 our composite (Jetson baseline) | **8.29** | 9.9 | 9.2 | 5.8 | 9.3 | 6.1 |
| 2 | S5 SWA-PF | **7.78** | 10.0 | 10.0 | 4.7 | 7.8 | 4.5 |
| 3 | S3 tile-matching (Shuhaieva) | **4.53** | 6.0 | 3.8 | 3.1 | 5.0 | 4.0 |
| 4 | S1 koksalan/gnss-denied-nav | **4.25** | 6.9 | 3.8 | 0.0 | 4.8 | 4.8 |
| 5 | S2 uav-geolocalization (CAEVL + VIO) | **2.38** | 0.0 | 0.1 | 10.0 | 0.0 | 2.5 |
| 6 | S4 hmakelin/gisnav | **0.79** | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 5.3 |

**Best for each purpose.**

| Purpose | Best | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Highest accuracy (lowest accepted-fix median, fix rate over 20 %) | S3 | common 1 Hz set, synthetic NIDAR-like |
| Highest coverage at 50 m (recall@50) | S5 | recall over all frames |
| Lowest latency under the constrained replay | S2 | 1-2 CPU cores, CPU only (no Jetson) |
| Best autopilot integration (SITL outcome score) | S6 | SIM-2..SIM-7, 3 seeds |
| Best for Jetson-class deployment (edge-fit score) | S2 | latency, throughput, memory; NOT measured on a Jetson |
| Most robust over feature-poor terrain and weather | S5 | precision, blur/haze windows, worst terrain class |
| Easiest to adopt (setup effort) | S5 | minutes + 10 per failed step |


**Recommendation for the NIDAR system.** Build the NIDAR baseline on the **retrieve → match → PnP → consistency gate → tracking** structure that S6 implements, with S6's permissive-licence parts (MegaLoc, XFeat, OpenCV; confirm the LighterGlue weight licence), fed by the compass and barometer hints. On the synthetic data it was the only complete pipeline: 92 % of frames fixed, 0.4 m median, 100 % precision, a 100 % mission-completion rate in SIM-2, SIM-4 and SIM-7, and a 0.9 s step on a 2-thread CPU. **Treat this as a design direction, not a verdict:** (1) S6 is our own composite, written and tuned (gate thresholds, tile size, crop) on the very frames it is scored on, with no held-out set; (2) video and map come from the same imagery, so the real appearance gap is untested; (3) nothing was measured on a Jetson, ONNX/TensorRT export of the matcher failed on CPU, and in the 5 Hz real-time replay it processed only 21 % of the frames on two threads and 13 % on one core; (4) it needs a heading and height hint, which were noise-free here. S5 (particle filter on semantic labels) was the second most accurate and the most robust to blur and haze (93.5 % fixed), but it needs an odometry source, converges only after about 10 s, takes several seconds per step on this CPU at 20,000 particles (the first step 37 s) and its labels here came from a substitute map, so it fits a GPU companion computer, not a CPU-only edge board. S1's gate and tracking ideas are already inside S6; S1 itself retrieved poorly with pretrained weights (22 % of frames, all in the first 44 s). S3 is a good reference for the plain two-stage idea but has no rotation handling and no gating; S2 (VIO plus map fixes) failed with our under-trained encoder and a VIO substitute, so it is neither supported nor refuted by this test; S4 could not be run. Whichever solution is chosen, the autopilot side needs a velocity or odometry aid: even ideal 5 m-noise fixes cannot bridge a 20 s gap with our position-only EKF configuration (SIM-3 failed for every row, including the control).

**What could not be tested.** The real NIDAR video and its telemetry (we used a synthetic NIDAR-like flight); any field or non-synthetic imagery with a seasonal or lighting gap to the map; the fallback datasets MAFS 200 m, MUN-FRL and ALTO (unreachable) and the UAV-VisLoc reproduction; any GPU run and any Jetson run (no Jetson number in this report is measured); TensorRT; OpenVINS inside S2 (built but not run: the Docker image export ran out of disk); S4 (GISNav) in any form: the stack could not be stood up here (6.9 GB image, PX4/Gazebo/QGC build, GPU and X11, 50 GB); S5 on the MAFS dataset and the cross-area test; the YFS90 item (no code exists) and the STHN item (thermal imagery only); a fully closed-loop SITL in which each solution's output is recomputed from the simulated vehicle's own camera view (we used Mode B with precomputed estimates); take-off with GPS already denied (SIM-6 cuts GPS at the start of cruise); roll/pitch/attitude errors in the hints (they are noise-free).

### 2.3 Deviations from the runbook (all of them)

1. **Synthetic video, not NIDAR** (above). The reference map is the very imagery the frames were rendered from, so there is no seasonal, lighting or resolution gap between query and map. This makes matching **much easier than in the field** and several solutions return implausibly small errors (for example S3 verified fixes at 0.07 m); we checked this against the metric code and the data alignment and it is genuine, a consequence of identical pixels.
2. **Data defect found and fixed during the run.** The first render used a body-fixed camera on a quadcopter that pitches −30° in cruise, so frames were strongly oblique (runbook: nadir or near-nadir). We re-rendered with a stabilised nadir camera and **re-ran every primary test**. The oblique results are kept in `results/<sol>/nidar_oblique/` and discussed as a stress result (S5: 106.8 m median error without rectification; S6: nadir assumption failed completely; S2: near chance).
3. **1 Hz subsampling.** Several tests ran on every 5th frame (1 Hz, 153 frames) because CPU time per frame is 5-35 s for S1, S3 and S5; each result names its frame count. The master comparison uses the **same 153 frames for every solution**.
4. **CPU only, no Jetson.** The constrained replay is an approximation: the process is pinned to 1-2 cores with `taskset`. No number in this report is a Jetson measurement.
5. **Degraded or substitute components**, each flagged where it appears: S1 uses pretrained DINOv2-base (the author's fine-tuned weights are unpublished); S2's VIO layer is our substitute (OpenVINS built but could not be run) and its CAEVL encoder is under-trained; S5's semantic map is our substitute from the repo's SegFormer.
6. **SITL is Mode B (video in the loop), not closed loop.** The vehicle flies the A→B→C→D mission in SITL; the solutions' estimates were precomputed offline on the recorded video. At each recorded frame position the bridge passes the solution's *error vector for that frame* applied to the SITL vehicle's true position as a `GPS_INPUT` fix. A solution's output is never recomputed from the SITL vehicle's own view, and its compute latency is not modelled except in SIM-4 (added 200 / 500 ms). SIM-6 (cold start) starts the GPS cut at the beginning of cruise instead of before take-off, because there are no ground-level frames.
7. **Fix feed rate** follows each solution's run: 5 Hz (S6, S2, S1 tracking run) or 1 Hz (S3, S5), without modelling the seconds of CPU time per fix.
8. **Not run** (reasons in the chapters): S4 (stack could not be stood up: 6.9 GB image pull ran out of disk, PX4/Gazebo/QGC needs a GPU, X11 and 50 GB), S1/S2/S3/S5/S6 fallback datasets, S2 with OpenVINS, TensorRT anywhere, GPU runs, Jetson runs, S7 items other than Bearing-UAV.

### Analysis written by the solution's test agent (from the code actually run)

### S1 analysis: koksalan/gnss-denied-nav on synthetic NIDAR-like data

All numbers below come from runs under `results/s1/nidar/<run-id>/` (harness `metrics.summarize`, same metric code as the other solutions). Data: **synthetic NIDAR-like** nadir render (gimbal-stabilised, 200 m AGL, 12 m/s, 1280x800 gray, 0.18 m/px), reference map Esri z19 0.283 m/px. **The video was rendered from the same map, so the appearance gap is optimistic.** Weights are the **pretrained (not fine-tuned) DINOv2-base: every S1 result is DEGRADED** (the author's fine-tuned weights are not published). CPU only, 2 threads, box shared with other agents (latencies are inflated and noisy; the lead's alone-run numbers supersede them). Query keypoints limited to 1024 (repo default 2048) to make CPU runs feasible.

#### 1. How it works (from the code that ran)
`adapter.py` -> `gdnav.localizer.Localizer.localize` per frame:
1. **Prior geometry**: the frame is rotated north-up by the compass yaw (`query.query_warp`, `heading_sign * yaw + offset`) and scaled to a fixed ground size from barometer height / focal length; a circular mask of 140 m diameter (inscribed circle of our frame) is cut. Without heading and height the method cannot start (it assumes north-up and known scale).
2. **Retrieval** (global mode only): DINOv2-base (CLS + GeM pooled patch tokens, 1536-d, L2-normalised) of the 224 px north-up patch; dot product against the 1225 pre-embedded map tiles (50 m stride); top-10 tiles. (Exact search done by a torch matmul; FAISS is not used in the localizer.)
3. **Fine matching**: SuperPoint keypoints of the warped query (up to 2048; we used 1024) are matched with LightGlue against a 450 m window of keypoints precomputed for the whole map (`MapFeatures`, kept in RAM), for each candidate; RANSAC fits a similarity transform (rejects rotation >15 deg or scale change >25 %), the candidate with most inliers wins.
4. **Pose**: inlier matches go to a homography RANSAC (4 px) and planar PnP (IPPE + LM refinement) on the ground plane: camera position (lat/lon), height above ground and off-nadir tilt.
5. **Confidence**: fix is trusted with >= 25 inliers.
6. **Consistency gate** (`sim/visual_gps.py::consistency_gate`, copied verbatim into the adapter): needs >= 50 inliers (>= 80 when no fix accepted for 5 s, "degraded"), |PnP height - baro| <= 8 m, |PnP tilt - IMU tilt| <= 4 deg (tilt skipped in degraded mode).
7. **Tracking mode**: once a fix is accepted, the next frame skips retrieval and matches only one 600 m window around the previous fix (`track_window_m`); a gate rejection keeps the prior, a "genuinely lost" frame (< 25 inliers) clears it and the next frame searches globally again.
8. Not in the adapter (out of scope): visual odometry between fixes (LK optical flow, `odometry.py`), ArduPilot GPS_INPUT bridge (`sim/visual_gps.py`), learned confidence model, detection/planning. The repo's "Lucas-Kanade fills gaps" part is therefore **not evaluated**; between fixes our adapter reports no position.

#### 2. Data-flow stages (for the diagram)
camera frame (gray->RGB) + compass yaw + baro height -> **north-up/scale warp (OpenCV affine, circular mask)** -> **DINOv2-base embedding (PyTorch, HF transformers)** -> **tile-DB top-10 (dot product; DB built offline from map tiles, 1225 x 1536 float)** -> **SuperPoint (LightGlue pkg) on query** -> **LightGlue match vs precomputed map keypoints window (x10 candidates, or x1 in tracking)** -> **RANSAC similarity (OpenCV)** -> **homography RANSAC + planar PnP IPPE/LM (OpenCV)** -> **consistency gate (baro height, IMU tilt, inlier count)** -> accepted fix lat/lon/height -> (repo, not run here) EKF3 via MAVLink GPS_INPUT. Tracking feedback: accepted fix -> prior window for next frame.

#### 3. Results (synthetic NIDAR-like, nadir)
Fix rate counts accepted fixes over ALL frames; precision = accepted fixes within 50 m (all accepted fixes were within 8 m in every run, so precision is 100 % and false fixes = 0 everywhere).

| Test | run id | frames | accepted | fix rate | median err | p95 | max | false fixes >50 m | latency p50 (loaded CPU) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1-T1 global search, no prior, 1 Hz subsample | S1-T1-20261023-s0 | 153 (stride 5) | 34 | 22.2 % | 1.40 m | 7.05 m | 7.6 m | 0 | 34.0 s |
| S1-T2 tracking after first lock | S1-T2-20261023-s0 | 153 | 45 | 29.4 % | 1.50 m | 5.06 m | 5.9 m | 0 | track 9.7 s / global 18.4 s |
| S1-T2full tracking, full 5 Hz (**SITL file**) | S1-T2full-20261023-s0 | 764 | 221 | 28.9 % | 1.56 m | 4.01 m | 7.4 m | 0 | track 5.4 s / global 9.1 s |
| S1-T5 tracking, gate OFF | S1-T5-20261023-s0 | 153 | 46 | 30.1 % | 1.53 m | 5.43 m | 5.9 m | 0 | - |
| S1-T6a no baro, no heading (nominal 200 m, heading 0) | S1-T6a-20261023-s0 | 77 (stride 10) | 16 | 20.8 % | 1.66 m | 4.30 m | 6.6 m | 0 | 12.3 s |
| S1-T6b baro kept, heading removed | S1-T6b-20261023-s0 | 77 | 16 | 20.8 % | 1.69 m | 4.46 m | 5.3 m | 0 | 10.2 s |
| S1-T9 failure injection, early windows (tracking) | S1-T9-20261023-s0 | 61 (t<=60 s, 3 dropped by the injector) | 26 | 42.6 % | 1.34 m | 4.87 m | 5.9 m | 0 | 11.0 s |
| S1-T9late injection after lock is lost anyway | S1-T9late-20261023-s0 | 153 | 35 | 22.9 % | 1.30 m | 3.67 m | 5.9 m | 0 | 13.2 s |

Notes on each test:
* **T1 (global, 1 Hz)**: the headline: **only 22 % of frames get a fix**, all inside the first 44 s (leg A->B, plus a few frames). Median 1.4 m on the fixes it makes (optimistic: same map). Time to first fix 0 s. T1 at 5 Hz (764 frames x ~35 s each) was not run: ~7 h of CPU. As agreed in the brief we used 1 Hz; **the 5 Hz estimates.csv for SITL is `S1-T2full` (tracking enabled, 5 Hz), not a no-prior run**. In tracking mode the lead should expect position only until t = 44.2 s; afterwards S1 outputs nothing (accepted = False) for the rest of the flight.
* **T2 tracking**: a tracking frame costs about half of a global frame (5.4 vs 9.1 s on the quieter box, 9.7 vs 18.4 s in the loaded run): no DINOv2, one LightGlue call instead of ten. Fix rate rises 22 -> 29 % (the 1 s gaps in haze are not bridged; lock is lost at t = 45 s and never regained).
* **T5 gate off**: no change in false fixes (0 -> 0) because there were no wrong matches to reject; the gate rejected one correct fix (t = 45 s, 33 inliers < 50, degraded rule 80). On this data the gate is neutral to slightly harmful; its value (author: rejected all 16 fixes > 50 m off) cannot be shown because the failure mode here is "no match", not "wrong match". Inlier counts of correct fixes are 127-172, far above the 25 vs 50 thresholds, so the 25-inlier rule alone already separates them.
* **T6 no hints**: fix rate 16/77 (20.8 %) for both variants versus 19/77 (24.7 %) for T1 at the same even-second frames (3 fewer fixes, error unchanged). Because the baseline only localises on the first leg where the true heading is ~0 deg (north) and the height is the nominal 200 m, **the test cannot show the dependence on hints**: it only shows the method tolerates heading errors < 15 deg and height errors of a few metres, and it silently depends on those hints elsewhere (heading error > 15 deg is rejected by the similarity gate). Without the barometer the height/tilt part of the gate is not available (only the inlier count).
* **T9 failure injection** (tracking mode, 1 Hz; windows 3-9 s wrong heading +90 deg, 12-20 s 50 % random frame drop, 33-38 s low light (gain 0.12, gamma 1.8, noise), 40-45 s synthetic Gaussian blur sigma 8 px; video blur 21-31 s, haze 49-69 s):
  * wrong heading +90 deg: lock lost at the first corrupted frame (t = 3 s), no false fix accepted (rotation > 15 deg is rejected); global search re-acquired at the first correct frame (t = 9 s): **recovery time 0-1 frame (1 s)**.
  * 50 % frame drop: **no effect**: the last fix stays as prior and tracking resumed at the next frame (recovery 0 s; fixes 12, 16...).
  * low light: lock lost at once (t = 33), no fix during the 5 s window, re-acquired globally at t = 38 (first clean frame): recovery 1 s after the window.
  * blur sigma 8: lock lost (t = 40), at t = 45 a correct but weak fix (37 inliers, 2.9 m) was rejected by the degraded gate (needs 80) and lock was never regained before the natural haze (49 s): **no recovery within 15 s** (here it is the retrieval, see below).
  * natural blur 21-31 s: T2 (tracking) got fixes on 9 of 18 frames inside the video blur windows, T1 (global) on 2 of 18 (all haze frames: 0 of 41 in both).
  * In T9late (injections at 35-45 s etc.) lock was lost at the blur (35 s) and never regained.
* **T3 real-time, T4 constrained**: implemented, not run (lead runs alone). **T4 export attempt** (single process CPU, 2 threads, loaded box; results/s1/nidar/S1-T4-20261023-s0/t4.json):
  * DINOv2-base retriever: torch fp32 944 ms -> ONNX Runtime fp32 602 ms (max abs diff 4e-7, 346 MB) -> ORT dynamic INT8 214 ms (90 MB) **but INT8 embeddings cosine to fp32 only 0.58: unusable** (the author uses "sensitivity-aware" INT8, not reproduced; not tried).
  * SuperPoint: only the dense CNN exported (800x1280 input): torch 2.59 s -> ORT 1.44 s; NMS/top-k/descriptor sampling remain python. No TensorRT / Jetson path (author states none).
  * LightGlue: TorchScript ONNX export fails twice (`IndexError: list index out of range` in torch.onnx symbolic helper, opset 16 and 17, with adaptive depth/width disabled); `torch.onnx.export(dynamo=True, opset 18)` works (after installing onnxscript), 46.6 MB, fixed depth (no early exit): torch 2.40 s -> ORT 2.12 s for 512 x 1024 keypoints (lightglue_retry.json). Adaptive pruning is lost in the export.
  * Overall, one tracking frame ~ SuperPoint 3 s + LightGlue 2-3 s on 2 CPU threads: ~6 s per fix at best, ~1/30 of the 5 Hz frame rate; real-time is not reachable on this CPU without a large model/resolution cut.
* **T7 fallback datasets**: not run. Attempt: GitHub UAV-VisLoc readme reachable (links to Baidu, blocked); HF search found mirrors `haiduonghuynhle/UAV_VisLoc_dataset` (one 17.7 GB zip, AGPL tag) and `Demyd/UAV_VisLoc_dataset` (empty), `VERYBC/XIAN_Visloc` (not checked): too large for the disk allowance, so nothing fetched. A single flight could perhaps be range-extracted from the zip; not attempted.
* **T8 SITL**: lead.

Plausibility checks (results/s1/alignment_check.txt): shifting the truth by +-0.1 s makes the error worse (1.56 -> 1.8-1.9 m), so time alignment is right; mean bias N 0.01 m, E -0.66 m; fixes come from image matching (PnP height 196.7 m vs baro 197.1 m), truth is only used by the driver for hints (baro, yaw) and by `metrics.py`. The 1-2 m error is credible for same-map rendering with 0.5 m/px matching; real-imagery appearance gap will make it much worse (the author's own median is 24 m).

#### 4. Failure analysis (frames in results/s1/figures/failures/t<T>.png: north-up query | expected tile at truth | top-1 retrieved tile; stats in failures.json)
| t (s) | condition | what happened | cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25 | video blur 21-31 s (peak 3 px) | no fix in global mode; the true tile has retrieval rank 23/1225, top-10 closest tile 311 m away | blur removes texture -> DINOv2 descriptor drifts; retrieval miss |
| 52 | haze 49-69 s | no fix; true tile rank 15 (top-10 nearest 162 m) | haze/low contrast; retrieval miss |
| 60 | haze | true tile IS rank 1 (8 m) but 0 inliers | haze contrast kills SuperPoint keypoints/LightGlue matches |
| 75 | clear air, forest/river | true tile rank 1 (12 m), 0 inliers | vegetation/water texture, gray query vs colour map -> few repeatable keypoints (see t75.png) |
| 100 | blur 95-104 + haze 95-107 | true tile rank 212 (nearest top-10 53 m) | combined degradation; retrieval miss |
| 130 | haze 125-134 | true tile rank 11 (just outside top-10), top-1 887 m away | haze; the fine-tuned retriever is exactly what is missing |
| 145 | clear | true tile rank 4 (26 m) but 0 inliers | matching failure on low-texture terrain (second half of the route) |
Summary of causes: (a) pretrained retrieval misses the right tile in the 10 candidates (blur/haze, ranks 11-212); (b) even with the right tile at rank 1, the SuperPoint+LightGlue stage finds 0-6 inliers on forest/water/haze; (c) after the lock is lost at t = 45 s the system never regained it in the remaining 108 s. By terrain: 0 accepted fixes after t = 44.2 s over ~108 s / ~1.2 km of path.
Frames with < 25 inliers in the gate counted as "genuinely lost" and cleared the tracking prior, so one haze frame forces an expensive global search that itself usually fails (no gap bridging; the repo's LK odometry would be needed).

#### 5. Comparison with the author's claims
| claim (README) | ours | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| median 24 m, 97 % within 100 m on held-out real UAV-VisLoc flights, whole-map search without prior (fine-tuned DINOv2) | median 1.4 m on the fixes made, but only 22 % of frames get a fix (global); the README's own *pretrained DINOv2-B + LightGlue* row is 30 m median / 69 % / 75 % (fix rate numbers) | **not reproduced / partly consistent**: our weights are the author's "pretrained" baseline, which the author also reports as much weaker (top-1 retrieval 18 %). Our accuracy is optimistic (same map); our coverage is much lower than 69 % because of blur/haze, a 140 m footprint (the author's 250 m patch has more context) and gray-vs-colour imagery |
| 6.3 m median error with GNSS jammed (SITL, Gazebo, EKF3 fusion), 840 m without | not run by us (SITL by the lead) | not tested |
| VO halves worst-case error (86 -> 32 m) | VO not run (adapter excludes it) | not tested |
| consistency gate rejected all fixes > 50 m off | no wrong fixes occurred, gate neutral/slightly harmful (1 correct fix rejected) | cannot be confirmed on our data |
| fast path: 24 fixes/s | 0.1-0.2 fixes/s on 2 CPU threads (GPU claimed) | not reproducible on CPU; ~100-200x slower |
| no Jetson/TensorRT | confirmed; ONNX export works for DINOv2 and (dynamo) LightGlue, SuperPoint partial; dynamic INT8 breaks the descriptor | consistent |
Differences: synthetic data, nadir stabilised 200 m, different camera (FOV 60 deg), pretrained weights, CPU.

#### 6. Verdict
* Strengths: very good accuracy when a fix exists (1-2 m here; PnP gives height and tilt that can be cross-checked with baro/IMU, a nice sanity gate); drift-free absolute fixes; clean modular code, matches its documentation; tracking mode halves the cost; heading and frame-drop faults are handled gracefully (no false fixes at all in any test); extensive training/evaluation scripts.
* Weaknesses: with off-the-shelf DINOv2 only ~1 frame in 4 gets a fix and nothing after t = 44 s; heavy dependency on compass heading (+-15 deg) and baro height; no published weights (cannot be used as delivered); heavy compute (needs GPU; 9-35 s per frame on 2 CPU threads); nothing between fixes without the VO part; thresholds tuned on one flight; SuperPoint weights are non-commercial; requires EPSG:4326 GeoTIFF.
* Use when: a GPU-equipped companion computer, a fine-tuned retriever for the operating area/season, reliable compass + barometer, fixed-wing/multicopter at moderate altitude over textured terrain, and a flight controller that accepts a second GPS. Not when: Jetson-class hardware without porting, low-texture terrain (forest, water, haze), no compass, or the weights cannot be trained.
* Risks observed: lock loss is silent and permanent in haze (no recovery for 108 s); gate rule "degraded" demands 80 inliers, which rejects good fixes after a gap; a wrong heading hint (>15 deg) blocks all fixes; prior gets cleared by any weak frame; memory ~2.4-3 GB; build 15 min on CPU for 1.9 km^2 (scales with area); harness-side: frame sorting by string.

#### 7. Files
`adapter.py` (Adapter + MapShim + gate), `driver.py` (T1..T9 driver, injection, subsampling, realtime mode), `t4_constrained.py`, `t4_lightglue_retry.py`, `failure_figs.py`, `run_all.sh` (queue used), `camera.json`, `lock.txt`, `SETUP.md`. Oblique-camera calibration runs of the discarded first data set: results/s1/nidar_oblique/ (body-fixed 30-degree-oblique camera: stress case only, 12-frame calibrations: fix on 2/12 frames, errors 1.5-3.5 m).

#### 8. Lead commands (run alone, serial, from /home/user/Nexmesh/gpsdenied-eval)
```
E=solutions/s1_gnss_denied_nav
# S1-T3 real time (5 Hz, 153 s wall, drops frames while busy)
OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 $E/env/bin/python $E/driver.py --id S1-T3 --mode realtime --config '{"query_kp":1024,"tracking":true}'
# S1-T4 constrained: ONNX variant timings (set threads / taskset for the constrained profile)
OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 taskset -c 0,1 $E/env/bin/python $E/t4_constrained.py --id S1-T4 --threads 2
# and constrained replay of the pipeline itself
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 taskset -c 0 $E/env/bin/python $E/driver.py --id S1-T4rt --mode realtime --config '{"query_kp":1024,"tracking":true}'
```
SITL estimates: `results/s1/nidar/S1-T2full-20261023-s0/estimates.csv` (5 Hz, 764 rows; accepted only for t <= 44.2 s). The tile index cache must exist (`cache/`, ~135 MB, git-ignored, on this machine); first start otherwise takes 15 min.


### Setup account

### S1 setup: koksalan/gnss-denied-nav (commit 572b9ffe..., see COMMIT.txt)

CPU: Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz, 4 cores shared (we used 2 threads, `nice`), 15 GB RAM, no GPU. Python 3.12 (uv venv; system python is 3.13).
Wall-clock from clone to first working output (frame 0 localised to 1.0 m): about 25 min (of which 15 min is the one-off tile index build). Total agent time including all tests: roughly 9 h (CPU-bound). Failed or changed steps: 6 (listed below).

#### Commands that worked
```
export UV_NO_CACHE=1                       # disk is tight (cleaned 2 GB uv cache afterwards)
cd solutions/s1_gnss_denied_nav
uv venv --python 3.12 env && . env/bin/activate
uv pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu     # torch 2.14.1+cpu
uv pip install "transformers>=4.45" faiss-cpu rasterio opencv-python-headless numpy scipy pandas matplotlib tqdm \
   kornia timm onnx onnxruntime scikit-learn joblib pymavlink imageio "lightglue @ git+https://github.com/cvg/LightGlue.git"
uv pip install onnxscript                  # only for the LightGlue ONNX (dynamo) export attempt
uv pip freeze > lock.txt                   # 74 packages
# first run builds + caches the tile DB and map keypoints (15 min), later runs start in ~20-40 s:
OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 nice python solutions/s1_gnss_denied_nav/driver.py --id S1-T1 --stride 5 --config '{"query_kp":1024}'
```
Skipped on purpose (out of scope): ultralytics/YOLO, stable-baselines3, gymnasium, fastapi/uvicorn (detection, RL planner, ground station). Not needed for localisation.

#### Weights (DEGRADED)
* Retriever: the repo has NO released fine-tuned weights (`outputs/` is git-ignored; README only shows training commands that need UAV-VisLoc, hosted on Baidu). Training was not feasible: no VisLoc data on disk (a 17.7 GB HF mirror `haiduonghuynhle/UAV_VisLoc_dataset` exists but exceeds the disk allowance; free disk was ~2.7-13 GB) and CPU fine-tuning of DINOv2-B would take far longer than 45 min.
* So: **pretrained `facebook/dinov2-base` (HF, 86.6 M params, 346 MB fp32 ONNX / ~330 MB HF cache), pool `cls+gem`, no fine-tune. All S1 results are flagged DEGRADED.** The author's own table (README) gives pretrained-DINOv2-B top-1 retrieval of only 18.2 % vs the fine-tuned model; we reproduce that weakness.
* SuperPoint `superpoint_v1.pth` (5 MB) and LightGlue `superpoint_lightglue` (45 MB) are downloaded by the `lightglue` package from github.com/cvg/LightGlue releases.

#### Index build (map data/nidar/map_esri_z19.png), recorded in cache/build_*.json
* Map resampled once from Web-Mercator to a linear lat/lon grid in RAM (the repo requires an EPSG:4326 GeoTIFF; `MapShim` in adapter.py replaces `SatelliteMap`). Native 0.283 m/px kept; the repo itself resamples to 0.625 m/px (retrieval tiles, 224 px) and 0.5 m/px (SuperPoint keypoint map) and warps each camera frame to the same scale, so no resampling to the camera GSD (0.18 m/px) is needed. Ratio map/camera = 1.57; camera -> 0.5 m/px is a 2.77x down-scale.
* 1225 tiles (140 m patch, 50 m stride), 1536-d descriptors (cls+gem), descriptor DB 7.5 MB. Build time 685 s (DINOv2-B on CPU, 0.56 s/tile under load). The onboard localizer does exact dot-product search with `torch` (`db @ q`), NOT FAISS; FAISS (`IndexFlatIP`, same exact search) appears only in `gdnav/evaluation.py` and `scripts/eval_int8.py`. README's "FAISS index" is therefore only partly accurate.
* SuperPoint keypoints of the whole map precomputed once: 4970x4970 px image at 0.5 m/px, 47 958 keypoints (up to 2600 per 1024 px tile), 124 MB in RAM, build 202 s.
* Peak RSS of a replay process ~2.4-3 GB.

#### Camera config (camera.json, repo format of configs/camera_visloc*.json)
`focal_px` 1108.51, `heading_sign` +1, `heading_offset_deg` 0 (the video has image-up = heading; verified: matches succeed at 133-172 inliers with 1 m error on the first leg; the repo's VisLoc configs use sign -1 for their dataset). `patch_m` = 140 m (the repo default 250 m would exceed the inscribed circle of our 1280x800 frame at 200 m: 800 px x 0.18 m = 144 m).

#### Failures / deviations (each counted)
1. `SatelliteMap` needs an EPSG:4326 GeoTIFF -> wrote an in-memory shim (no GeoTIFF re-reads, as README recommends).
2. Repo default patch 250 m does not fit our camera -> 140 m.
3. CPU cost: stock config (top-10 rerank, 2048 query keypoints, 450 m windows) took 35-60 s/frame at the beginning (contended box; SuperPoint upsamples the 280 px query to 1024 px; ten LightGlue runs ~3 s each) -> `query_kp=1024` for all runs (calibration runs in results/s1/nidar_oblique/ and S1-calib-nadir; on oblique-data calibration frames 2048 vs 1024 keypoints gave 1.0 vs 1.5 m on frame 0 and the 2048 run died before finishing, so equivalence is only weakly checked). Lower `search_m=250` broke correct matches (inliers 11 vs 37), rejected.
4. harness/run_replay.py sorts frame names as strings (100.0 before 20.2) -> driver sorts numerically; yaw hint is in degrees (adapter has `yaw_unit`).
5. First data set (body-fixed, 30 deg oblique camera) replaced by the lead with a nadir render after ~3 h of my runs; those runs were stopped and not used (calibration logs kept in results/s1/nidar_oblique/).
6. A calibration process (2048 keypoints) died (probably OOM while other agents were running); rerun not needed.

#### Reproducibility verdict
Setup with the repo as published: reproducible for localisation code; **results of the author are not reproducible** because weights, training data and dataset links are not published (Baidu only), and no pinned requirements (requirements.txt has only lower bounds such as `torch>=2.4`; `lightglue` from git HEAD). Seeds: no stochastic component in inference except RANSAC (OpenCV, default seeding); `--seed 0` set for numpy/torch, T9 frame-drop uses numpy rng seed 0.

## S2 uav-geolocalization (CAEVL + VIO)

> **Substitute inputs:** the VIO layer is **our substitute** (phase correlation + compass yaw + barometer), not OpenVINS (it built but could not be run within the disk limit). The CAEVL encoder is ours, trained about 50 minutes on a CPU for 2 epochs on 1,800 tiles (the authors: up to 20 epochs on ~250k tiles on a GPU).

### Analysis written by the solution's test agent (from the code actually run)

### S2 analysis (uav-geolocalization: CAEVL + VIO + fuse.py)

Data label: **synthetic NIDAR-like** (map and frames from the same Esri imagery; optimistic). **VIO layer = OUR-VIO-SUBSTITUTE, not OpenVINS** (OpenVINS builds, was never run; see SETUP.md). **Primary data = gimbal-stabilised NADIR render (data/nidar). The earlier body-fixed 30-degree-oblique render is kept as a stress result (appendix, results/s2/nidar_oblique/).** **CAEVL encoder = our 2-epoch CPU-trained model (about 50 min), far weaker than the authors' GPU model.** The central result must be read with both caveats.

#### How it works (from the code run)
Stages:
1. Map prep (offline): north-up tiles cut from the reference map at a fixed ground size (60/120/240 m, stride half a tile), resized to 256x256 gray.
2. Edge descriptor: OpenCV Canny (70/200) on the tile -> CNN encoder of CAEVL (`caevl.ae` encoder, 37.5 M params, 1024-d, PyTorch CPU) -> L2-normalised descriptor. Computed once per tile and stored as a float32 matrix (3.7 MB for 900 tiles).
3. Training (offline, reference imagery only): stage 1 autoencoder reconstructs Canny maps; stage 2 VICReg pulls together a clean tile and a randomly degraded copy (rotation, zoom, blur, vignette, lens mask) with variance/covariance terms to avoid collapse.
4. Query: camera frame -> (our adaptation) rotate to north-up by compass yaw and scale by baro altitude (the nadir data needs no tilt correction; for the oblique data a full ground-plane rectification through IMU-estimated roll/pitch was used) -> same Canny + encoder -> cosine nearest neighbour (matrix product; `faiss` not needed at this size) -> tile centre = absolute fix (corrected for the camera-axis offset).
5. VIO (relative motion): author uses OpenVINS (MSCKF, ROS 2). We used OUR-VIO-SUBSTITUTE: north-up ground images + `cv2.phaseCorrelate` between consecutive frames + compass yaw + baro height.
6. Fusion (`fuse.py` causal): keep a trailing 30 s buffer of fixes with the VIO position at each fix time; RANSAC on two-fix similarity transforms (inlier radius 60 m, at least 3 agree) keeps only mutually consistent fixes; all accepted fixes ever seen are fitted with a least-squares similarity (scale, yaw, offset) once they span 300 m; output = transform applied to the current VIO position. Modes `align` (offline windowed refit) and `ekf` (4-state filter, chi-square gate) are alternatives. The retrieval score is never used.
7. Optional corridor search: restrict candidate tiles to a disc around the motion prior.

#### Results (primary: nadir data; runs under results/s2/nidar/<id>/)
| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| S2-T1 VIO only (substitute, 764 frames at 5 Hz, path 1464 m) | final error 7.9 m, RMSE 5.0 m, 5.4 m per km of path (0.54 %). T1b degraded (3 deg yaw bias, -4 % scale): final 29.0 m, RMSE 36.5 m, 19.8 m/km. Uses noise-free truth yaw and baro altitude, so this is optimistic; real OpenVINS drift unknown. |
| S2-T2 retrieval only (120 m tiles, 900 tiles, 764 frames, full map) | recall@50 m 3.8 %, @100 m 4.6 %, @250 m 9.2 %; median error 656 m, p95 1146 m; true tile median rank 64 of 900; true place in top-20 within 100 m: 43.5 %. Clear weather 6.8 % @100 m; haze 0 %, blur 0 %, blur+haze 0 %. Near chance. |
| S2-T3 fused causal, full-map search (estimates.csv for SITL) | fused RMSE 798 m vs VIO alone 5.0 m (whole flight); after warm-up (t >= 25.4 s) 874 m vs 5.5 m. Final 316 m vs 7.9 m. Accepted at arrival 84 fixes, 7.1 % precise (raw precision 4.6 %); fitted scale 2.95, yaw -30 deg (wrong). Fusion is far worse than VIO alone. |
| S2-T3c fused with a 200 m corridor around the motion prior | fused RMSE 116 m (whole flight; 129 m after warm-up at 29 s) vs 5.0 m VIO. Raw fixes in the corridor are 31.8 % within 100 m and consensus accepts 301 fixes with 36.9 % precision, but 69 % wrong is still enough to corrupt the fitted transform. |
| S2-T4 fuse.py batch modes on the T3 logs | causal as shipped (with its non-causal pre-filter) RMSE 804 m; align (offline) 576 m; ekf 837 m; VIO alone 5 m. The offline bound does not rescue it. |
| S2-T5 consensus off | RMSE 580 m (fit yaw -17 deg, scale 2.88) vs 799 m with consensus on; consensus helps slightly but >95 % of fixes are wrong and wrong fixes agree with each other. Streaming port reproduces the adapter to 2e-8 m. |
| S2-T6 corridor off vs on (T2 run, prior = VIO substitute) | off: recall@100 4.6 %, median 656 m, 900 candidates, 0.08 ms. 200 m radius: recall@100 35.6 % (@50 24.1 %), median 121 m, 35 candidates, 0.03 ms. 300 m radius: 18.6 % (@50 13.6 %), median 198 m. The gain is mostly the geometric prior (median error is about the corridor scale), not better descriptors; encode (about 190 ms on the loaded 2-thread box) dominates, search time is negligible. |
| S2-T7 tile size at 1 Hz (153 frames), stride T/2 | 60 m: 3721 tiles, recall@50 2.6 %, @100 4.6 %; 120 m: 900 tiles, 3.9 % / 4.6 %; 240 m: 196 tiles, 0 % / 0 % (stride 120 m caps accuracy near 85 m and one 240 m query is mostly black corners). All near chance, no tile size is meaningfully better. |
| S2-T3x sanity (synthetic fixes with 30 m noise, NOT CAEVL output) | The fusion layer cannot help a 5 m VIO: with the substitute VIO, 40 % good fixes still gives RMSE 5 vs 5 m (-9 %) and 10-20 % good fixes make it worse (168 m, 20 m). With a degraded VIO (RMSE 37 m): 20 % good -> 12 m (67 % lower), 40 % good -> 18 m (50 % lower), 10 % good -> 125 m (worse). Consensus off: 344-608 m at every rate. |
| S2-T8 real-time / constrained | implemented (`run_s2.py t8`), NOT run (lead runs). |
| S2-T9 fallback dataset | not run: MUN-FRL unreachable, no open mirror known. |
| S2-T10 SITL | not run by S2. |

#### Does fusion beat VIO alone? Is the 36 % reduction reproduced?
No, and not reproduced. On nadir data our VIO substitute is already very good (RMSE 5 m, 0.5 % of path), so there is little drift for fixes to remove, and our under-trained encoder (4.6 % of raw fixes right) feeds the fusion mostly wrong fixes, so fused RMSE is about 160x worse (798 m vs 5 m). Author claim: causal RMSE 617 -> 392 m (-36 %) with a real OpenVINS that has a 34-40 % scale error, on MUN-FRL where 18 % of fixes are right. Our VIO layer is not comparable with that, so relative gain is judged only as fused vs VIO-alone here: negative. The sanity test shows the consensus + similarity-fit layer helps (50-67 % lower RMSE) only when the VIO is poor (tens of metres) and 20-40 % of fixes are good; it fails at 10 %. Claimed retrieval R@1 @100 m 48-53 % (ViLD), 17.7 % (MUN-FRL): ours 4.6 %. We cannot separate method quality from our training budget (50 min CPU, 1800 tiles, versus GPU, about 250 k tiles): that is the main confound. 13.3 Hz on CPU: not measured (lead T8); single encode about 190 ms on our loaded 2 threads.

#### Failure analysis (T2/T3, 120 m model; crops query | expected | matched in results/s2/figures/failures/)
By condition (recall_by_condition.csv): clear 512 frames 6.8 % recall@100; haze 160 frames 0 %; blur 46 frames 0 %; blur+haze 46 frames 0 %. Top-1 error and true-tile rank:
- t=10 s (clear, take-off leg): 1090 m, rank 2, score 0.995 (confident, wrong; nearly right ranking).
- t=24 s (blur): 920 m, rank 313; edges wiped by blur.
- t=40 s (clear): 302 m, rank 218.
- t=58 s (haze 0.6): 657 m, rank 21.
- t=74 s (clear, over river/bridge, low texture): 650 m, rank 100.
- t=98 s (blur + haze): 892 m, rank 240.
- t=128 s (haze 0.55): 745 m, rank 320.
- t=145 s (clear, last leg): 957 m, rank 46.
Causes: under-trained encoder; scores uninformative (wrong matches score 0.98-0.995, as the README says); repetitive dense rooftops; blur/haze suppress Canny edges; stride 60 m caps accuracy at about 42 m. Fusion failures: everything after warm-up (t > 25 s) follows a wrong transform; error 300-1350 m.

#### Verdict
Strengths: tiny index (0.8-15 MB), encoder-bound runtime with negligible search, appearance-invariant concept, honest docs, design that ignores the retrieval score; a corridor prior is a cheap large gain (4.6 -> 35.6 % recall@100). Weaknesses: needs a well-trained encoder per area and altitude (no released weights; a CPU hour is not enough); fuse.py is a batch tool tuned to one flight (its "causal" CLI applies a non-causal pre-filter; VIO-alone baseline is aligned with fixes from the whole flight; accepted fixes are re-appended every step); needs yaw, altitude (and attitude); degrades under blur/haze; consensus latches onto consistent wrong matches and cannot improve a good VIO. Use when a GPU-trained encoder exists for the terrain and altitude, fix hit rate is at least 20 %, and VIO drift is large. Do not use as shipped on this data.

#### Risks observed
Harness: `run_replay.run` sorted frames as strings (breaks temporal adapters; S2 uses its own driver); hint yaw is in degrees (adapter `yaw_unit='deg'`). Disk/memory pressure (stage-2 training 4-8 GB RAM; docker export ENOSPC). Under-trained model must not be read as the method ceiling.

#### Appendix: oblique stress result (results/s2/nidar_oblique/, "body-fixed 30-deg-oblique camera")
Before the dataset fix the camera was body-fixed with 30 deg nose-down pitch. S2 handled it by IMU tilt estimation (complementary filter, median error 0.1-0.2 deg, transients to 13 deg) plus ground-plane rectification. Results then: VIO substitute RMSE 61 m (final 19 m; the error was a 40-60 m offset from the take-off tilt transient); retrieval recall@100 2.0 %, median 688 m; corridor 200 m 23.7 %; fused RMSE 790 m (fuse.py batch causal 1057, align 434, ekf 790) vs 61 m VIO; consensus off 675 m; tile size 60/120/240: 4.6/2.0/2.0 %; sanity with good fixes at 20-40 % gave 49-59 % lower RMSE than that 61 m VIO. Conclusion identical: the weak encoder breaks fusion; a poorer VIO (as in the oblique case) is where fusion has room to help. Old figures: results/s2/figures_oblique/.

#### Lead commands for T8 (run alone; outputs in results/s2/nidar/S2-T8-<mode>-20261023-s0/)
```
cd solutions/s2_uav_geolocalization && . env/bin/activate
OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 python run_s2.py t8 --mode realtime --threads 4
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 taskset -c 0 python run_s2.py t8 --mode constrained --cores 0 --threads 1
```
Main SITL file: results/s2/nidar/S2-T3-20261023-s0/estimates.csv (VIO-only until t=25.4 s, then fused; fused is worse than the VIO-only track in S2-T1-20261023-s0/estimates.csv, which is the better input for SITL).


### Setup account

### S2 setup log (uav-geolocalization = CAEVL + OpenVINS + fuse.py)

Primary results (results/s2/nidar/) are on the gimbal-stabilised nadir data; the earlier body-fixed oblique results are in results/s2/nidar_oblique/ (stress result). All results: **synthetic NIDAR-like** data (map and frames both from the same Esri imagery, so the appearance gap is optimistic).
**The VIO layer in every result is `OUR-VIO-SUBSTITUTE`, NOT OpenVINS** (see "OpenVINS" below).

#### Commands that worked
```
git clone <caevl fork> caevl_src ; git clone -b alto_integration <open_vins fork> openvins_gpl/src   # both clone fine via the git proxy (curl/gh API 403, git works)
python3 -m venv env && . env/bin/activate
pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch torchvision
pip install numpy opencv-python-headless pyyaml tifffile tqdm timm einops faiss-cpu loguru scikit-learn Pillow scipy pandas matplotlib gdown   # gdown is imported but missing from caevl requirements.txt
python make_train_tiles.py 1800                      # 1800 train + 240 val reference tiles (60/120/240 m, random positions, 256 px)
cd caevl_src
python caevl/ae/train.py -c ../configs/ae_nidar.yml            # stage 1 (1 epoch)
python caevl/ft_stage/train.py -c ../configs/stagetwo_nidar.yml  # stage 2 (epoch 1), then again with --load-weights (epoch 2)
cd .. ; S2_TILT=on is needed only to reproduce the oblique runs.
python run_s2.py t1 ; python retrieval_eval.py --tag S2-T2 --tile 120 --corridors 200,300 --vio <T1 vio_track.csv>
python run_s2.py t3 ; python run_s2.py t3 --tag S2-T3c --corridor 200 ; python post.py t4|t5|t9 ; python make_figs.py
retrieval_eval.py --tag S2-T7-tile{60,120,240} --tile {60,120,240} --step 5
```
Wall clock from clone to first working output (a retrieval number): about 95 min, dominated by CPU training and a loaded machine.

#### CAEVL training (CPU, budget < 60 min, spent about 50 min)
Reference-only training as in the README: stage 1 autoencoder on Canny edge maps (172.5 M params, encoder 37.5 M, latent 1024), stage 2 VICReg on clean/degraded tile pairs. Data: 1800 tiles from the NIDAR map (mixed 60/120/240 m footprints so one model serves the T7 sweep), val 240. Seed 0.
| step | epochs | batch | wall | train loss | val loss |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stage 1 (L2, no DINOv2 perceptual loss) | 1 | 32 | 16.5 min | 0.220 | 0.170 |
| stage 2 VICReg | 1 | 32 | 16.0 min | 24.5 | 19.0 |
| stage 2 VICReg (resumed) | +1 | 32 | 16.0 min | 21.3 | 17.97 |
Total about 49 min. The authors trained on GPU for up to 20 epochs on ~250k tiles; we used 2 epochs-equivalent on 1800 tiles, so this encoder is severely under-trained (see ANALYSIS.md: retrieval is near chance). Logs: results/s2/training/. Stage-1 checkpoint was deleted for disk (resume of stage 2 needed `load_weights_backbone: False`).

#### Tile database
Own script (`s2core.Retriever`; the repo's `munfrl_map_tiles.py` is MUN-FRL-filename specific and `caevl` tile tools target IGN data). North-up tiles, stride = tile/2, 256 px, descriptors L2-normalised, computed once.
| tile | stride | tiles | index | build time (2 threads, loaded box) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 m | 30 m | 3721 | 15.2 MB | 285 s |
| 120 m (default) | 60 m | 900 | 3.7 MB | 68-85 s |
| 240 m | 120 m | 196 | 0.8 MB | 16 s |

#### Adaptations needed (not in the author's code)
1. **Camera tilt (oblique data only).** The first dataset version was body-fixed, pitched -30 deg in cruise. For that data `s2lib.query_crop_att` resampled frames onto a north-up ground plane through full attitude (roll/pitch from our own complementary filter on imu.csv, `ahrs.py`, set `S2_TILT=on`); those results are in results/s2/nidar_oblique/. The current primary data (data/nidar) is a gimbal-stabilised nadir render, so roll=pitch=0 (default), only compass yaw (hint, in DEGREES) and baro altitude are used.
2. **Streaming fusion.** fuse.py is a batch CLI. `s2core.StreamFuser` re-implements the loop of `causal_mode` step by step, importing `causal_consensus`, `fit_similarity`, `rotz` unchanged from repo/tools/fuse.py. It deliberately omits the CLI's whole-flight consensus pre-filter (non-causal). Re-run from logs it reproduces the adapter output to 8e-9 m.
3. Start position (take-off point) is assumed known (config `start_latlon`); the VIO is anchored there. Before the fusion transform exists (warm-up) the adapter returns the VIO-only estimate with flag `warmup_vio_only` and accepted=True.

#### OpenVINS (3 attempts / outcome)
1. Docker daemon was not running; started `dockerd` in background (works, overlayfs). Docker Hub reachable (`ubuntu:20.04`, `ros:foxy-ros-base` pulled).
2. Built the fork (branch alto_integration) in `ros:foxy-ros-base` (Ubuntu 20.04, ROS 2 Foxy; the repo's own Dockerfile uses Galactic and a heavy desktop image, avoided for disk). `colcon build` **succeeded**: ov_core, ov_data, ov_eval, ov_init, ov_msckf, 5 packages in 30 min 21 s (`openvins_gpl/build_summary.txt`). So the "does it build" check passes (last upstream release v2.7 May 2023).
3. Second attempt after the nadir data fix (lead asked for one more try): compiled again OK (5 packages, 30 min 53 s, `openvins_gpl/build_summary2.txt`) but the image export failed with ENOSPC again (3.1 GB free; the copied source tree carries the 'ov_data' dataset CSVs). Not retried a third time: it would need a .dockerignore for ov_data, another 30 min of CPU and ~5 GB shared disk, plus a ROS bag run. First failure: the `docker build` image export then failed with ENOSPC (disk was 2.7 GB free; lead asked to prune). I removed the image and cache and did NOT rebuild (another 30 min CPU + ~5 GB). A rosbag writer (`openvins_gpl/make_bag.py`) and NIDAR configs (`openvins_gpl/cfg/`) were prepared but never run. **No OpenVINS trajectory exists**; all VIO numbers are from OUR-VIO-SUBSTITUTE. Risk noted for a future attempt: cruise at constant velocity with a 5 Hz nadir camera and 50 Hz IMU is a weak case for MSCKF initialisation/scale.

#### Failed steps (count 7)
1. curl/gh to the forks: 403 (git clone works). 2. `dockerd` killed by my own `timeout 20` -> restarted with nohup. 3. gdown missing import. 4. first stage-2 launch OOM-killed at batch 64 (8 GB) -> batch 32. 5. `exec(train.py)` has no `__file__` -> ran as script. 6. Deleting stageone.pth broke the resume (FileNotFoundError) -> `load_weights_backbone: False`. 7. Docker export ENOSPC.

#### Reproducibility verdict
Partly. Code installs and trains with small fixes (gdown, CPU device in configs). No released weights; no tile/VIO scripts for non-MUN-FRL data; fuse.py only runs as a batch CLI on files. Our numbers are reproducible from seed 0 (fuse RANSAC seeded; retrieval deterministic).

#### Documentation rubric (0-3)
install steps work as written 1 (requirements incomplete, CUDA defaults in configs, hard-coded author paths); config explained 2 (configs well commented); results reproducible 1 (no checkpoint, depends on author's data/paths); algorithm described 3 (README, fuse.py docstrings are detailed and honest).

### Analysis written by the solution's test agent (from the code actually run)

### S3 tile-matching pipeline: analysis

All numbers: **synthetic NIDAR-like, nadir (stabilised) frames**, 1 Hz subset (153 frames, every 5th frame) unless stated; metrics from `harness/metrics.py`; run folders `results/s3/nidar/<run-id>/`. The query frames are warps of the same map the tiles are cut from, so appearance matches the map far better than in the field.

#### How it works (from the code that ran: adapter.py, which mirrors the notebook cell by cell)
1. Offline: the map is resampled so one pixel equals the camera ground resolution, cut into 1024x1024 px tiles with stride 512 (361 tiles), and every tile is turned into a 384-d DINOv2-small embedding (518x518, class token, L2-normalised). Index build 700 s on a loaded CPU, 0.6 MB.
2. Per frame: the frame is embedded the same way and compared with all tiles by cosine similarity; the top 5 tiles are candidates.
3. ALIKED extracts up to 1,024 keypoints from the frame and each candidate tile (only the top-1 if its similarity is ≥ 0.82; at most 3 candidates; stop early at 25 inliers). LightGlue matches them and USAC_MAGSAC fits a homography with a 5 px threshold.
4. With ≥ 6 inliers the frame centre is projected through the homography into the tile and then into the map (lat, lon): a **verified fix**. Otherwise the centre of the top-1 tile is returned: a **fallback** (our adapter marks it `accepted = false` and scores it separately).
5. There is no motion model, no use of heading or height, and each frame is independent.

#### Results
| Test | Run id | Result |
|---|---|---|
| S3-T1 as published, no hints (153 frames) | S3-T1-20261023-s0 | verified fixes on 52 frames (34.0 %), median error 0.07 m, p95 452 m, **precision@100 m 86.5 %** (7 of 52 verified fixes are wrong, up to 990 m); recall@10/50/100 m 29.4 %; fallback on 101 frames with median error 730 m (recall@100 m 11.8 %) |
| S3-T2 verified vs fallback separately | same run | verified: 0.07 m median; fallback: 730 m median, so the fallback is a coarse guess and is never a usable fix |
| S3-T1b OUR EXTENSION: frames de-rotated north-up with the compass yaw (not the author's method) | S3-T1b-20261023-s0 | 86 verified (56.2 %), recall@50 m 49.0 %, precision@100 m 87.2 %, p95 776 m |
| S3-T3 ablation: no scale normalisation (raw frame scale, map not resampled; 144 tiles) | S3-T3-noscale-20261023-s0 | 60 verified (39 %), precision@100 m falls to 60.0 %, recall@50 m 23.5 % (from 29.4 %): the 1024 px tile size only works when map pixels match the camera ground resolution |
| S3-T4 retrieval depth (1 / 3 candidates tried of top-5 / 10 tried of top-10) | S3-T4-top1, S3-T1, S3-T4-top10 | verified 49 / 52 / 61; recall@50 m 27.5 / 29.4 / 30.7 %; precision@100 m 85.7 / 86.5 / 77.0 %; p50 step 9.9 / 14.1 / 9.1 s (loaded CPU, not comparable): more candidates add few extra fixes and more wrong ones |
| S3-T5 terrain (substitute semantic map classes under the true position) | report section 3.4 | recall@50 m: building 18.9 %, vegetation 12.5 %, water 50.0 %, mixed 38.0 % (the 26 "water" frames are mostly the river bank and bridge region where strong edges exist; this is a class from our substitute labels, not real land cover). Fixes drop in blur/haze windows (recall@100 m 22.2 % vs 34.4 % clear) |
| S3-T6 real-time and constrained replay | serial runs, report section 3.5 | step time is 6-14 s on this CPU: the solution cannot keep up with a 5 Hz stream (see table) |
| S3-T7 fallback dataset replay and UAV-VisLoc subset 06 reproduction | – | **not run**: UAV-VisLoc is a 17.7 GB archive (Google Drive / one Hugging Face zip), too large for the disk allowance; MAFS unreachable |
| S3-T8 OUR EXTENSION: constant-velocity Kalman filter over the fixes (not the author's method) | S3-T1-20261023-s0-KF | mean step between consecutive outputs falls from 124 m to 13 m, but between-fix extrapolation drifts: median error 235 m, recall@50 m 37.9 % (raw verified fixes: 29.4 %). Smooths jumps, does not recover accuracy |
| S3-T9 SITL with a GNSS jam window | report section 4 | no scenario SIM-2..SIM-7 completes: the verified fixes arrive on 34 % of 1 Hz frames, the EKF raises its variance failsafe at about 68 s, the same as with no vision (SIM-1). With de-rotation (extension) fixes reach 56 % of frames and the EKF survives until about 110-117 s, but no mission completes |

**Plausibility check.** A 0.07 m median error on verified fixes looks too good. We checked the metric code on a synthetic trajectory (unit tests) and the frame alignment (the verified homographies have a median of 400 inliers and project the frame centre to within the rendering noise). The query is the map itself after a warp, blur/haze and noise; with 400 matching keypoints sub-pixel accuracy (0.18 m/px) is expected. It does not predict field accuracy.

#### Failure analysis (T1; `results/s3/nidar/S3-T1-20261023-s0/failure_diag.json`; images with Esri crops are kept local and not committed)
Nine failed frames, chosen across the clear, blur and haze periods: t = 14, 23, 29 s (heading ≈ 0°: clear, blur, blur), 54, 57, 61 s (heading ≈ 85-90°: haze), 73, 76 s (heading 89°, clear), 95 s (heading 89°, blur).
- **The retrieval is mostly right.** The tile that contains the truth is rank 1-4 of 361 in 6 of the 9 frames (rank 1 at t = 61 s and 73 s even with the pipeline's own un-rotated input), rank 6 at t = 76 s, and rank 9-10 in the blurred frames at t = 29 and 95 s (rank 12-14 after de-rotation).
- **The verification fails.** Those frames give 0-5 inliers, below the 6 needed, so the pipeline falls back to the tile centre (about 700 m wrong on average here because tiles are 185 m wide and the first-ranked tile is not always the right one).
- **Cause 1: rotation.** From t ≈ 50 s the vehicle flies east (heading 90°) and then south-west; the frame is rotated by the heading but ALIKED/LightGlue are not rotation-invariant. At t = 73 s (clear air, rank-1 tile) there are only 5 inliers. De-rotating by the compass raises the fix rate from 34 % to 56 % (T1b).
- **Cause 2: blur and haze.** Fewer keypoints survive; in the blur window t = 23-29 s there are 5 inliers or fewer, and retrieval degrades (rank 9-14 at t = 29 s and 95 s).
- **Cause 3: a verified-but-wrong fix.** 7 of the 52 verified fixes are far off (up to 990 m) because the 6-inlier threshold is low and a wrong tile that shares repeated building texture can pass it; no gate (height/baro/IMU) exists to reject them (precision@100 m 86.5 %).

#### Comparison with the author's claims
| Claim (UAV-VisLoc subset 06, real imagery, flights ≥ 405 m) | Ours (synthetic NIDAR, 200 m, same-map imagery) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Top-1 tile recall 70 %, top-5 85 % | not measured as a separate metric; the true tile is in the top 4 in 6 of 9 failed frames | not compared |
| Median error 3.85 m, mean 14.20 m | verified fixes only: median 0.07 m; every frame counted (verified + tile-centre fallback): median 172.5 m, mean 380 m | **not reproduced** for an all-frames median; the verified-only median is better because the images share pixels with the map |
| Hit rate ≤ 50 m 88.5 %, ≤ 100 m 92.1 %, ≤ 500 m 96.8 % | all frames: 34.0 % / 41.2 % / 62.7 % (T1); with de-rotation 49.0 % / 49.0 % / 69.9 % | **not reproduced**; far lower on our rotating-heading video, which the notebook's north-up dataset does not contain |
The author's own caveat holds: forest, fields and water give few matches. Our video also rotates with the heading, which is not mentioned in the README.

#### Verdict
- **Strengths:** shortest and simplest of the pipelines (one notebook); no training; the algorithm is easy to read; verified fixes are very accurate when they exist; every component is a pretrained public model.
- **Weaknesses:** no rotation handling (the author's data is north-up); a 6-inlier acceptance threshold with no height/attitude gate; a tile-centre fallback that is a 100-700 m error rather than a rejection; no tracking so every frame pays the full retrieval and matching cost (6-14 s per frame on CPU); notebook only, no licence.
- **Use when:** frames are north-up (or de-rotated with a compass) and the scale matches the map, an offline or high-latency fix source is acceptable, and a gating layer (EKF innovation test, baro, tracking) sits behind it. **Do not use** as the only position source on a moving platform, on an embedded CPU without a GPU, or where a licence is needed.
- **Risks observed:** tile size is in pixels, so the scale ratio is a hidden requirement (T3: precision drops to 60 % without it); results come from a map that equals the query source; no licence.


### Setup account

### S3 setup log (ShuhaievaPolina/UAV-Visual-Localization-via-Satellite-Imagery)

Repo commit: see `COMMIT.txt` (e63334eda6359391fc9f3700671aac1dbac6f342). Versions: `lock.txt` (torch 2.14.1+cpu, timm 1.0.30, lightglue from git, rasterio 1.5.2, numpy 2.5.2, Python 3.13). All results are **synthetic NIDAR-like** data.

Wall clock from clone to first working output: about 45 min (of which 11 min is the one-off DINOv2 tile-embedding build, 361 tiles, on a loaded CPU). Failed or changed steps: 3.

#### Commands that worked
```
python3 -m venv env; export PIP_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/pipcache
env/bin/pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
env/bin/pip install timm opencv-python-headless rasterio numpy pandas matplotlib pillow tqdm "git+https://github.com/cvg/LightGlue.git"
env/bin/python run_s3.py --tag S3-T1 --step 5            # offline replay, 1 Hz, as published (no hints)
env/bin/python run_s3.py --tag S3-T1b --step 5 --derotate # OUR extension: de-rotate frames north-up with the compass yaw
```
`adapter.py` re-implements the notebook's classes (`GeoCalibrator`, `SatelliteTileDatabase`, `EdgeLightGlueMatcher`, `run_evaluation_pipeline`) one-to-one (1024 px tiles, 512 stride, DINOv2-small `vit_small_patch14_dinov2.lvd142m`, top-5, sim threshold 0.82, up to 3 candidates, early stop at 25 inliers, USAC_MAGSAC at 5 px, ≥6 inliers else top-1 tile-centre fallback). The map is first resampled so one pixel equals the camera ground resolution (ratio 1.569 = 0.283 / 0.1804 m/px; recorded in `metrics.json` as `scale_ratio`).

#### Failures and fixes
1. **The project is a Colab notebook, not a runnable package.** It mounts Google Drive for the UAV-VisLoc zip and uses `!pip`. Fix: the class code was transplanted into `adapter.py` (a reimplementation of the same logic; nothing else changed).
2. **ALIKED weights download returned HTTP 403** (`github.com/.../raw/main/models/aliked-n16.pth` through the proxy). Fix: the same file from `raw.githubusercontent.com` (clone of Shiaoming/ALIKED) copied into the torch hub cache. The weights were later deleted by another job's cache clean-up and restored the same way.
3. **Our own adapter bug**: a duplicate `derotate` keyword in the config dict and a sign error in the de-rotation angle (fixed before the reported runs).
Not a failure but a trap: the notebook feeds the drone image **unrotated**, the query images of its dataset are north-up; frames from a heading-up camera are rotated by the vehicle heading and the pipeline has no rotation handling.

#### Reproducibility verdict
Partly reproducible. The code is short and the algorithm is described, but there is no script, no config file, no pinned requirements (`requirements.txt` has no versions and lists `torch` without CPU/GPU guidance), no seeds other than `seed_everything(42)`, and the dataset needs a Google-Drive archive. Our runs are reproducible from the commands above (no stochastic parts apart from OpenCV's RANSAC).

### Analysis written by the solution's test agent (from the code actually run)

### S4 GISNav - ANALYSIS (static; the stack was not run, see SETUP.md)

All statements below come from reading repo/ros/gisnav (commit f2c72641) and repo/docs, not from execution. No metrics exist for S4. Data would have been "synthetic NIDAR-like".

#### How the matching works (plain language)
GISNav does not predict where the drone is by itself. It assumes the autopilot already supplies an approximate position, heading and altitude (MAVROS NavSatFix, pose, gimbal attitude). From that and the camera intrinsics, BBoxNode computes the ground footprint of the camera field of view (padded to a square) and GISNode asks the onboard WMS server (OWSLib GetMap, layers "imagery" and "dem", EPSG:4326, JPEG) for that area; it only re-fetches when the old map overlaps the new footprint by less than 85 percent. StereoNode converts the map to grayscale, rotates it by the vehicle heading (in 5-degree steps) so north-up map matches the camera orientation, and crops it to the camera image size, because the matcher is not rotation invariant. Query frame: TwistNode detects SIFT keypoints (RootSIFT descriptors). PoseNode detects SIFT on the map crop (cached while the map is unchanged), matches query and map descriptors with LightGlue (kornia LightGlueMatcher, SIFT variant, confidence filter 0.5), requires at least 15 matches, looks up per-point height from the DEM layer, and solves camera pose with cv2.solvePnPRansac (only 10 RANSAC iterations, no inlier check or reprojection-error gate that we could find). The resulting global pose is a noisy, discontinuous "absolute" measurement. In parallel TwistNode does visual odometry: SIFT + brute-force knn match between successive frames, PnP, scaled to metres using altitude; this is smooth but drifts. Two robot_localization EKFs fuse them (global EKF: absolute pose + differential VO). The fused odometry goes to UORBNode (px4_msgs SensorGps via micro-ROS/XRCE-DDS), or NMEA/UBX nodes, as a fake GPS fix (fix_type 3, fixed covariance values) so PX4 treats it as a GNSS source. Only the SIFT branch is used; the CPU path is designed to reduce keypoints (1024) and LightGlue layers.

#### Architecture stages
1. Camera (gscam / ROS Image + CameraInfo) and autopilot state (MAVROS: NavSatFix, pose, gimbal attitude) - prior position/heading/altitude.
2. BBoxNode: FOV footprint on ground plane -> geographic_msgs/BoundingBox.
3. GISNode: WMS GetMap client (OWSLib, MapServer + PostGIS/GeoServer-style server) -> OrthoImage (RGB + 8-bit DEM).
4. StereoNode: grayscale, rotate by heading, crop to query size -> OrthoStereoImage.
5. TwistNode: OpenCV SIFT on query; BF-matcher VO between frames + PnP -> relative pose.
6. PoseNode: SIFT on reference, kornia LightGlue (PyTorch) matching, DEM lookup, cv2.solvePnPRansac -> absolute pose (ECEF via proj/affine from WMS CRS).
7. robot_localization ekf_local_node and ekf_global_node (5 Hz) fuse stage 5 and 6.
8. Extension nodes: UORBNode (px4_msgs SensorGps -> micro-ROS agent -> PX4 uXRCE-DDS), NMEANode, UBXNode.
9. Simulation environment (docker compose): PX4 SITL v1.14.2 + Gazebo Classic (San Carlos airport), QGroundControl, MapServer, PostGIS, micro-ROS agent.

#### Results table
| Test | Status |
|---|---|
| S4-T1 PX4 SITL, GPS off | not run: 6.94 GB gisnav image pull hit ENOSPC; PX4/Gazebo/QGC build and GPU/X11 requirement; 3 attempts (SETUP.md) |
| S4-T2 NIDAR replay | not run (no stack) |
| S4-T3 two map resolutions | not run |
| S4-T4 real-time/constrained | not applicable (nothing to run); no command for lead |
| S4-T5 fallback dataset | not run: dataset unreachable |
| S4-T6 ArduPilot SITL via sitl_bridge | not run: no estimates.csv. Note ArduPilot service in repo is marked "unmaintained ... does not work" in docker-compose.yaml; mock GPS output only via NMEA/UBX/uORB so a bridge would have to be a custom node |
| S4-T7 failure injection | not run. Static expectations: WMS down -> GISNode keeps polling/connect timer, PoseNode gets no new reference (stale map used until timeout); wrong prior -> map from wrong place, SIFT matches fail (<15) or give false PnP (no outlier gate) |

No failure-window frames were produced (nothing executed). Weather windows from data/nidar/weather.json were not tested.

#### Author claims vs reproduced
Project claims (README/landing page, no numeric claims): precise global position by comparing nadir frames to onboard GIS map; PX4 mission completes GNSS-free in SITL with `failure gps off`; simulation only, "do not use for real flights", "untested". Reproduced: nothing (not run). Demonstrated by project: only the Gazebo San Carlos airport demo video. Not reproduced because of resources, not because of a failure observed.

#### Verdict
Strengths: MIT, modular ROS 2 design, standard OGC WMS map interface (any GIS server), EKF fusion of drift-free absolute fixes and VO, PX4 integration without touching the GPS driver. Weaknesses: research prototype, explicitly sim-only; heavy dependency stack (Docker, ROS 2 foxy, PX4 v1.14, micro-ROS, NVIDIA GPU recommended; 50 GB disk); relies on autopilot prior position/heading/altitude (cannot do cold-start global localisation, and must stay within the fetched map); matcher is not rotation invariant (needs heading); SIFT + LightGlue is sensitive to appearance gap (season, haze, blur) and our nadir 200 m scenes; flat PnP with 10 RANSAC iterations and no visible outlier rejection; fixed covariance; ArduPilot support unmaintained; single main maintainer; no published accuracy figures. Static concern: `self._device == "cpu"` in pose_node.py compares a torch.device to a str, which is probably always False, so the CPU-limited matcher config may never activate (unverified). Use it as a reference design for WMS-fed map matching; do not use for flights or as a drop-in for ArduPilot. Licence MIT (SETUP.md table).

#### Risks observed
Disk/resource footprint (image set ~7 GB for gisnav alone), GPU dependency in compose files, no release/test evidence outside sim, mock GPS looks like real GNSS to the autopilot (fix_type 3, jamming/spoofing state unknown) so a wrong fix is trusted. Last release in earlier survey Aug 2024 (repo HEAD dated 2024-08-18).

### Analysis written by the solution's test agent (from the code actually run)

### S5 SWA-PF: ANALYSIS (CPU, synthetic NIDAR-like data, substitute semantic map)

READ FIRST (honest framing)
- All NIDAR numbers are on SYNTHETIC NIDAR-like frames (nadir re-render, 1280x800 gray, 200 m AGL) rendered from the SAME Esri map the filter matches against.
- The semantic MAP is OUR SUBSTITUTE: the repo's drone SegFormer-B0 (`logs/8_b0`) run on windows of `data/nidar/map_esri_z19.png` (resampled to 0.18 m/px, gray, 1280x800 windows), merged to the repo's classes, majority-pooled to 1 m/px (T5: 2 m/px). Frame labels come from the SAME segmenter on frames rendered from the same map, so map/frame agreement is optimistic. This is NOT the paper's U-Net map labelling (the paper's satellite labels cost >60 min per map image by hand annotation; no U-Net weights are shipped).
- Odometry is NOT ground truth: velocity (north/east/up) = finite difference of truth.csv + Gaussian noise (sigma 0.5 m/s north/east, 0.3 m/s up) and heading = truth yaw + N(0, 1.5 deg), passed through `Adapter.set_odometry(v_north, v_east, v_up, yaw_deg)` before each `step()` (the harness hints carry no odometry). The velocity is a world-frame vector, i.e. it presumes a compass/velocity source. Particle noise (adapter): sigma 8 m in x and y, 8 m altitude, 0.2 deg yaw per step, mean 0 (repo: mean +2, sigma 15 px).
- Replay is 1 Hz (every 5th frame, 153 frames), 2 threads, nice, CPU shared with 3-4 other jobs (load 8-11): latencies are inflated and NOT valid as an embedded timing figure. 5 Hz (764 frames) was not run: 5-10 s per frame x 764 = >1.5 h per run.
- Particle counts: 20,000 for the main run (the paper's number), 1,000 to 40,000 in the sweep; the repo's resampler keeps 80 % of the particles per frame down to a floor of 1000, so counts fall to 1000 after about 14 frames.

#### 1. How it works (written from the code that was run)

Plain language. The filter keeps a cloud of guesses ("particles"), each a guess of the drone's map position (x, y), altitude and heading. Every frame:
1. The drone image is turned into a coarse "what is this" picture by a small neural net (SegFormer-B0, 7 classes, repo weights `logs/8_b0`). Only four of its classes matter downstream: ground/other, building (roof and wall are merged: `pr==5 -> 1` in SWAPF.py), road, vegetation. Vehicle (4) and water (6) are produced but ignored by the weights.
2. The map is a satellite image that was labelled once, offline, with the same 4 classes (`label.png`). For every class a distance map is precomputed: for each map pixel, the distance (clipped at 100 px) to the nearest pixel of that class.
3. Each particle cuts out the piece of that class-distance map the drone would see from its guessed altitude (`cut = alt * cam_view * height_to_pix / 2` pixels each side), rescales it to 400x400 (so altitude changes only the cut size, not the comparison size), and compares it with the drone class image, which was pre-rotated in 100 steps of 3.6 deg (25 rotations x 4 quarter turns) and rescaled to 400x400. The score is the sum over pixels of "drone says class c here" x "distance to nearest class c in the map crop", multiplied by a weight that grows with distance from the crop centre (`wan`), plus a huge penalty if the crop sticks out of the map. Low sum = good match. Particle weight = 400*400 / (sum^2).
4. Particles are resampled by weight (80 % of them survive each frame, floor 1000), then moved with the odometry (distance and bearing of motion, heading change) plus Gaussian noise in x, y, altitude and yaw.
5. Position estimate: when the cloud's spread is below a tenth of its initial spread, the particles are clustered (DBSCAN) and the cluster centre is taken (`center()` in PFtool.py; it also prints the error against ground truth, which is only a diagnostic).

Initialisation (PFtool, hard-coded `init_method_mode`): 0 full random over map x, y, altitude and yaw; 1 layered (4 altitude floors, same xy/yaw); 2 xy sampled on building pixels ("semantic alignment").

##### What the "odometry" in SWAPF.py really is (leakage)
`SWAPF.py` reads `gps.txt` (ground-truth latitude, longitude, height, heading of every frame) and calls `particles.move(lat - old_lat, lon - old_lon, height - old_height, theta, old_theta)`. So the motion model receives the exact, noise-free ground-truth displacement, altitude change and heading of the drone, and the particle noise (gauss sigma 15 px in x,y, 8 m in z, 0.2 deg in yaw) is the only uncertainty. Initial particles are random (no pose leak), but the heading is known exactly after the first frame (all particles inherit the true heading change, the true heading offset is only found by the 100-way yaw search). `init_particles_goal`/`update_goal_1` put the ground truth in a "goal" particle used only for drawing. Hence the paper's 6.57 m is a filter with perfect relative motion and heading; there is no drift to fight. `center()` is commented out in the demo, so the demo as shipped saves overlay pictures only and outputs no estimate. Our replay replaces this with noisy telemetry odometry (see below).

#### 2. Architecture (data-flow stages)
1. Frame (BGR 1280x800) -> optional extension: ortho-rectification with IMU roll/pitch (used only for the oblique stress set).
2. SegFormer-B0 (PyTorch 1.10 CPU, 512x512 letterbox, 7 classes) -> per-pixel class image; roof merged into building.
3. 100 pre-rotated 400x400 4-channel binary class images (torchvision rotate x25 + rot90 x3), multiplied by the bowl weight; integral images (adapter speed-up; repo does the same sum per particle).
4. Offline: satellite map -> label.png (paper: U-Net-VGG, 4 classes; ours: same SegFormer) -> per-class clipped distance transforms (cv2.distanceTransform) + padded copies.
5. Particle array (N x 6: x, y, altitude, yaw, weight, cumulative weight); weight = 160000/sum^2; resampling by searchsorted (80 % kept, min 1000).
6. Motion update with odometry (distance, bearing, yaw change) + Gaussian noise.
7. Spread check + DBSCAN (scikit-learn) -> cluster centre (x, y, altitude, circular-mean yaw) -> lat/lon through map georeference; accepted only when converged and the main cluster holds >= 50 % of particles.
#### 3. Results (synthetic NIDAR-like, nadir frames, 1 Hz, seed 0 unless stated; metrics from harness/metrics.py `summarize`)

Frames: 153 for T2; 40 (t = 0..39 s) for T3/T4; 60 for T5. "converged and stays" = first accepted time after which every accepted fix is within 50 m (my own addition, from run_s5.py). Recall is over ALL frames, including the unavoidable convergence period.
