##### T3 particle sweep (initial particle count; seed 0; 40 frames; times under CPU load 8-11, 2 threads)
| initial N | accepted fixes | median err (accepted) | converged-and-stays<=50 m | first step | median step | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 18 % | 817.6 m (false lock, wrong) | never | 11.7 s | 5.3 s | 2255 MB |
| 5,000 | 8 % | 0.91 m | 37 s | 9.3 s | 4.5 s | 2247 MB |
| 20,000 | 75 % | 1.85 m | 10 s | 37.3 s | 9.5 s | 2337 MB |
| 40,000 | 75 % | 1.98 m | 10 s | 66.7 s | 8.3 s | 2293 MB |
Time per step is dominated early by the number of particles (about 1.5 ms per particle with my integral-image speed-up; the repo's own loop is about 17 ms per particle here) and later by a constant of about 4-5 s (SegFormer 1-3 s + 100 rotated label images + integral images). Peak RSS (about 2.3 GB) is mostly torch + SegFormer + distance maps; it barely depends on N.

##### T4 initialisation (n=5000, seeds 0,1,2, 40 frames; failure = no stable convergence (<=50 m) within 40 s)
| init | converge-and-stay time per seed | failures |
|---|---|---|
| full random | 37 s, none, 22 s | 1/3 never converged correctly within 40 s (seed 1: still 600 m off), |
| layered random (4 altitude floors) | none, none, none | 3/3 |
| semantic alignment (xy on building pixels) | none (616 m off), 10 s, none (3 wrong accepted fixes, 581 m) | 2/3, with false accepted fixes |
Caveat: only 3 seeds x 40 frames x 5,000 particles; at 20,000 particles full random converged in 10 s (T2, T3). With 5,000 initial particles the correct mode is often lost in the first resamples (80 % kept per frame, noisy odometry, coarse labels). Layered init gives 4 copies of each xy so it has 4x fewer distinct positions. False confident fixes exist (cloud collapses on a wrong place: spread below threshold but 500-800 m off): the spread/DBSCAN test is not a correctness test.

##### T6 scene classes (post-hoc on T2, converged frames only; class = share of OUR substitute map labels in the 100 m square under the true position; 'water' = segmenter label 6 >10 %, may be shadows/dark roofs, not verified water)
| scene | frames | median raw error | p90 |
|---|---|---|---|
| building >70 % | 53 | 2.82 m | 5.74 m |
| vegetation >40 % | 24 | 3.16 m | 8.41 m |
| water-labelled >10 % | 26 | 3.49 m | 5.30 m |
| mixed | 50 | 1.59 m | 3.08 m |
| blur windows | 18 | 2.01 m | 3.03 m |
| haze windows | 41 | 3.39 m | 6.12 m |
| clear | 103 | 2.01 m | 5.10 m |
No feature-poor breakdown was observed after convergence: because the particles move with (noisy) odometry and the map labels came from the same segmenter, a 4-class match survives low-texture windows; haze and vegetation are the worst (about +1.4 m median). The true breakdown risk is in the acquisition phase (below) not after lock.

#### 4. Oblique-frame stress results (first render, camera body-fixed, pitch -30 deg in cruise): results/s5/nidar_oblique
- S5-T2 as-is (20,000 particles): fix rate 65 %, median 106.8 m, p95 119.9 m, RMSE 103.3 m, recall@10 and @50 = 0 %. The filter locks, but on the image-centre ground point, which sits about 115 m behind the drone (200 m x tan 30 deg), so the error equals the geometric offset. Repo/paper estimate x, y, altitude, yaw only: roll/pitch are not modelled, so a tilted camera breaks it.
- S5-T2b with my ortho-rectification extension (IMU roll/pitch + baro with noise 0.5 deg / 1 m): the filter locked correctly at t=37 s (error 2.6 m) but lost lock after the first turn (about t=42 s; error 100-220 m for the rest; median 172 m): rectified oblique frames far from nadir are low resolution and distorted, and the turn changes tilt. Fix rate 55 %. Both runs are evidence for the feature-poor/robustness story, not the headline.
- register_check.txt / align_check_res1.0.json in that folder show the 107 m offset (template matching) that led to the data defect report to the lead.

#### 5. Failure analysis (nadir T2 plus sweeps; figures: results/s5/figures/failures/*.png = frame | map crop at TRUE position | map crop at ESTIMATED position)
1. t=0-9 s (T2): no fix, cloud still spread 300 m down to 30 m; random initialisation needs about 10 s (resampling shrinks 20,000 -> 1000). Cause: acquisition phase of a global filter; figure t=4.
2. t=74 s (veg, 11.3 m worst converged error): vegetation-dominated window; probable cause (not verified): tree/ground labels differ between map and frame labelling; figure t=74.
3. t=135 s (building, 7.6 m) and t=116 s (mixed, 5.1 m): probable cause (not verified): heading noise (1.5 deg) plus the 3.6 deg rotation quantisation; errors are only 5-8 m.
4. t=60 s and t=50 s (haze 48.9-68.7 s, 7.1 m and 4.8 m): low contrast, SegFormer labels shift; error rises from 2 to 3.4 m median but lock holds.
5. n=1000 initial particles (T3), init modes 1 and 2 (T4): false lock at 540-820 m; wrong cluster accepted (581 m, 3 fixes in init2/seed2; 817 m median in n=1000). Not weather related; cause: too few particles/modes lost during the first resamples, and acceptance test (spread < 10 % of initial) cannot detect a wrong mode.
6. Oblique set (section 4): 30 deg camera tilt, 115 m systematic offset; after rectification loss of lock at the turn (t about 42-50 s).
7. Blur windows (21.4-30.6 s and 94.7-103.9 s) caused no failure here (median 2.0 m): SegFormer labels are coarse anyway.

#### 6. Comparison with the author's claims
| Claim | Paper (MAFS, real, GPU) | Ours (synthetic NIDAR-like, CPU, substitute map) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| RMSE | 6.57 m | 3.53 m (T2, accepted fixes) | not comparable: synthetic, map and frames from the same imagery and segmenter; at 1 m/px labels and noisy (not GT) odometry; NOT reproduced on MAFS |
| recall@10 m | 97.4 % | 92.2 % over all frames (100 % of accepted frames <=11.3 m) | partly consistent in magnitude; same caveats |
| 20,000 particles in ~4.9 s on GPU | yes | 37 s first step (20,000), steady 5-10 s per frame at 1000 particles on a loaded 2-thread CPU; the repo's own per-particle loop is about 17 ms per particle (about 6 min per frame) | CPU is 8-75x slower; with my integral-image rewrite 1.5 ms per particle |
| works at several altitudes (4-DoF) | yes | altitude is a state (150-250 m search); not stressed (flight at 200 m) | not tested |
| memory efficient | no figure | peak RSS 2.3 GB at 1 m/px over 0.9 km x 0.9 km (1.7 GB at 2 m/px); mostly torch + SegFormer; per-class float32 distance maps (10 copies incl. padded) | note: scales with map pixels (full 1.9 km map at 0.5 m/px would need several GB) |
| roll/pitch not estimated | stated | breaks on a 30 deg tilted camera (115 m offset) | confirmed limitation |
| MAFS reproduction | 3 trajectories Hangzhou | not run | dataset unavailable |

#### 7. Verdict
Strengths: genuinely cheap map representation (4-class labels instead of image tiles or descriptors; a 1 m/px label map of 0.9 km square is under 1 MB), no map feature database, works with any segmenter that gives the 4 classes, tolerant to blur/haze after lock, fast convergence (10 s) with 20,000 particles, centimetre-to-metre-level when labels agree. Weaknesses: needs a relative-motion source with world-frame velocity and heading (the demo even uses ground truth GPS differences); needs consistent semantic labels on both sides (the paper's labelling is manual/U-Net; here the same segmenter on both which is optimistic); global start is slow and unreliable on CPU (n=1000-5000 often locks onto wrong places, acceptance test cannot tell); no roll/pitch handling; per-frame cost on CPU is seconds; shipped code is a demo (hard-coded Windows path and ground-truth motion, `center()` commented out); no licence declared; dataset unobtainable here.
Use when: a good odometry source exists (VIO or velocity+compass), a labelled map is available, and a GPU (or a rewritten vectorised filter) is used, as a coarse global relocaliser / drift reset. Do not use as the sole GNSS-denied localiser on a CPU companion computer, on tilted cameras, or in scenes where the segmenter cannot separate classes.
Known risks observed: false convergence; strong dependency on particle count (5,000 not enough here); disk/RAM scale with map pixels (map arrays are duplicated 10x as float32 distance maps); upstream Chinese comments, dead code and hard-coded modes; reproducibility 0 of 3 on data; no licence.
(failure PNGs contain Esri map crops: kept local only, not pushed)

#### Failures and fixes
- F1 `uv pip install torch` ENOSPC (shared disk full): removed uv cache, `--no-cache`, TMPDIR inside project. Retried twice.
- F2 `import torch` -> `No module named pkg_resources` (torch 1.10 needs it; new setuptools dropped it): `setuptools<70`.
- F3 Repo `update_particles` is a python loop of per-particle torch ops (4x400x400 float64 products): 35 s per frame for 2,000 particles under load (measured, dbg run), about 6 min per frame for 20,000. Fix (adapter side): `State.update_particles_fast`, an exact rewrite of the same weight formula using an integral image (verify_fast.py: max relative weight difference 1.3e-3 from nearest-neighbour block-boundary rounding). 20,000 particles then cost about 35 s per frame, 1,000 about 5 s (rotation set-up dominates).
- F4 `SegFormer_Segmentation` hard-codes `.cuda()`: constructed with `cuda=False` (config option exists, no repo edit). Loads state_dict with map_location=cpu: works. 2 threads, 512x512 input: about 1.5-2 s per frame on the loaded CPU.
- F5 `ParticleState.__init__` wants files `label.png`, `img.png` and `detail.txt`-derived list: adapter writes a temporary label PNG and a 4x4 dummy img.png (img only feeds an unused grayscale copy), passes `map_detail=[x_min,x_max,y_min,y_max,height_to_pix,...]` in local metres. Init mode is a local variable in `__init__` (cannot be selected from outside): adapter re-initialises particles itself with the three repo modes.
- Diagnosed late (not a setup failure but cost 1 h): the camera is body-fixed and SITL cruise pitch is -30 deg, so frame centre lies about 115 m behind the drone (see ANALYSIS). Repo (and paper) estimate x,y,altitude,yaw only.

#### Reproducibility verdict
Install steps work as written for the README's versions (CPU builds instead of cu113). Reproducing the paper numbers is impossible here (dataset on Baidu Pan only, partial). Demo script is not runnable without edits (hard-coded Windows path, GPU, imshow). Weights shipped in repo (logs/8_b0, 15 MB, sha256 prefix 8de15426fbd2b4f4); the satellite U-Net weights for map labelling are NOT shipped (no code for the U-Net in repo besides the SegFormer; map `label.png` is expected from the dataset).

### Analysis written by the solution's test agent (from the code actually run)

### S6 "our composite" -- analysis

All results: synthetic NIDAR-like data (gimbal-stabilised nadir render, 200 m AGL, 12 m/s, 764 frames at 5 Hz). The reference map is the SAME Esri z19 mosaic the video was rendered from, so the appearance gap is zero and accuracy is optimistic. CPU only (Xeon 2.1 GHz, 2 threads, box shared with other agents, load avg 5-9): every latency here is "measured under shared CPU load" and untrustworthy; the lead re-runs. NO Jetson, GPU or TensorRT number was measured; any Jetson figure quoted is from the survey and unverified.
"Our composite" is a baseline we built; it is not an existing project.

#### How it works (from the code that ran: s6lib.py, adapter.py)
Per frame, given hints (barometer height, compass yaw; roll/pitch = 0 for the nadir camera):
1. Rectify: ground-plane homography from attitude + baro height maps the 1280x800 frame to a north-up 1024x1024 canvas at map resolution (0.283 m/px; the camera GSD is 0.18 m/px so the frame is downsampled by 0.637; ratio recorded). Slight Gaussian blur before downsampling.
2. Retrieve: centre 384-px crop of the canvas, scaled 0.5 (192 px), MegaLoc descriptor (8448-d) -> FAISS IndexFlatIP over 625 map tiles (512 px, stride 256) -> top-5 tiles.
3. Match: XFeat (top 2048 keypoints, keypoints near the canvas black border dropped) vs XFeat features of a 1280-px map patch centred on the tile (cached) -> LighterGlue matches.
4. Geometry: USAC-MAGSAC homography RANSAC for inliers, then planar PnP (IPPE + LM refinement, camera K from camera.json, map pixels in metres on z=0) -> camera position (the fix), height, tilt, yaw.
5. Consistency gate: >=20 inliers, median reprojection residual <=3 px, |PnP height - baro| <= max(12 m, 10 %), tilt <= 50 deg, |PnP yaw - compass| <= 15 deg (tilt-vs-IMU check only when attitude is trusted; off here). First candidate that passes with >=70 inliers stops the loop, otherwise the best passing candidate is used; else accepted=False (never a guess).
6. Tracking window (T4 config `tracking=true`): after a lock, retrieval is skipped; a map patch is cut around the constant-velocity prediction and matched directly (single match, extra gate: jump <= 30 m/s*dt+40 m, >=15 inliers). 3 consecutive misses -> back to global retrieval.
Data-flow stages: frame -> [attitude/baro rectify, OpenCV] -> [MegaLoc ViT-B/14 DINOv2 backbone + SALAD aggregator, PyTorch] -> [FAISS flat IP] -> [XFeat, PyTorch] -> [LighterGlue, kornia] -> [MAGSAC homography, OpenCV] -> [IPPE planar PnP, OpenCV] -> [gate] -> [tracking state] -> lat/lon via map georef.
Structure follows hloc (retrieve-match-PnP); the gate/tracking ideas are from S1 reimplemented, no code copied.

#### Setup facts
Tile index: 625 tiles x 8448 float32 = 21.1 MB; build 1088 s on shared CPU (1.7 s/tile, first run, 2 threads under load 9); cached afterwards. DINOv2-small index: 625 x 768 = 1.9 MB, 61 s. MegaLoc 228.6 M parameters (0.87 GB weights). Peak RSS ~2.1 GB (XFeat+LG) / 2.5 GB (SP+LG).

#### Results (synthetic NIDAR-like, nadir; metrics from harness/metrics.py)
| Test | Run id | frames | fix rate | median err m | p95 m | max m | precision@100 m | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S6-T1 offline, global retrieval every frame, 5 Hz | S6-T1-20261023-s0 | 764 | 92.8 % | 0.41 | 1.09 | 6.76 | 100 % | estimates.csv for SITL |
| S6-T4 (offline accuracy run with tracking window) | S6-T4off-20261023-s0 | 764 | 95.3 % | 0.35 | 1.01 | 5.36 | 100 % | 736 track / 28 global frames; real-time run NOT done (lead) |
| S6-T3 XFeat+LighterGlue, 1 Hz | S6-T3-xfeatlg-20261023-s0 | 153 | 92.2 % | 0.39 | 1.01 | 2.87 | 100 % | median inliers 270; latency p50 0.94 s |
| S6-T3 SuperPoint+LightGlue, 1 Hz | S6-T3-splg-20261023-s0 | 153 | 100 % | 0.14 | 0.42 | 2.50 | 100 % | median inliers 507; latency p50 3.7 s |
| S6-T2 MegaLoc (1 Hz) | S6-T2-megaloc-20261023-s0 | 153 | recall@1 84.3 %, @5 95.4 % | | | | | embed p50 273 ms |
| S6-T2 DINOv2-small CLS+mean-patch (1 Hz) | S6-T2-dinov2s-20261023-s0 | 153 | recall@1 39.9 %, @5 63.4 % | | | | | embed p50 59 ms |
| S6-T5 variants (CPU only) | S6-T5-20261023-s0 | | | | | | | see below |
T2 criterion: a tile (512 px) containing the true footprint centre. Time to first fix 0 s (first frame accepted). Full-run latency p50/p95 (shared load): T1 1.39/7.0 s per frame, T4off 1.77/8.2 s (the tracking path re-extracts the reference patch uncached each frame, so it is not faster on this CPU; the saving is the avoided retrieval and extra candidates). Not comparable to a Jetson.
Fix rate is mostly bounded by our own gate (see failures): of 55 rejected frames in T1, 39 had a raw (rejected) pose within 5 m of truth, 5 were wrong by >50 m (haze), so the gate trades fix rate for 100 % precision.

T3 caveat: SP+LG is more accurate and robust on this data but 4x slower on CPU, and the SuperPoint weights are research-licence only. T2 caveat: our DINOv2-small baseline is untrained for VPR (CLS + mean patch tokens); the gap to MegaLoc is partly that.

|---|---|---|

Accuracy change of ONNX variants was checked on descriptor/feature outputs only, not end-to-end replay.

#### Failure analysis (T1; figures: results/s6/figures/failures/*.png = frame | expected map crop at truth | map crop at the pipeline's rejected estimate)
Fix rate by condition (T1): clear 99.6 %, haze 90 %, blur-only 19.6 %, blur+haze 100 % (blur+haze windows overlap at 95-104 s where gaussian blur was probably weaker than in the pure blur window 21-31 s).
1. t=21.4-30 s (blur window peak sigma 3 px): ~40 frames rejected by the residual gate (median residual > 3 px) although 200-280 inliers and raw error < 1 m (t=21.4: raw err 0.4 m). Cause: our gate threshold, not the geometry -> a loose gate would give ~+5 % fix rate; kept as run (no post-hoc tuning).
2. t=30.2 (end of blur): 24 inliers, raw error 23.6 m, correctly rejected (few inliers + residual).
3. t=52.4 (haze 49-69 s, strength 0.6): retrieval returned wrong tiles, 6 inliers, raw error 986 m, rejected by 4 gate checks. Haze lowers contrast so top-5 tiles missed.
4. t=56.0 and 57.2 (haze): same pattern, raw errors 1044 m / 1049 m, rejected (inliers 6).
5. t=55.0 (haze): 17 inliers, 20 m raw error, rejected (few_inliers).
Also 57.4 s: 7 inliers, 175 m. The tracking run bridges these windows (95.3 % fix, no wrong accepted fix) because the constant-velocity window supplies the location prior; global retrieval is what fails in haze.
No accepted fix exceeded 6.8 m error in T1 (precision@100 m = 100 %); accepted-fix precision is the strong point, fix availability under blur/haze the weak one.

#### Comparison with claims
- Survey "MegaLoc ~15 Hz and XFeat+LighterGlue 30+ Hz on Jetson Orin": NOT reproduced and not testable (no Jetson). On this 2-thread shared CPU: MegaLoc 3.8 Hz alone (265 ms), XFeat extract 4.4 Hz, LighterGlue match 3.6 Hz; end-to-end frame p50 1.4 s. Hardware classes differ by orders of magnitude, so no inference about Orin is drawn.
- No author accuracy claim exists for the composite itself (it is our design).

#### Verdict
Strengths: sub-metre median error on synthetic data, 100 % precision of accepted fixes, absolute (no drift), permissive licences for the main path (MIT/Apache; LighterGlue weight licence unconfirmed), modular (retriever/matcher swappable, ONNX path for XFeat/MegaLoc works). Weaknesses: heavy for CPU (MegaLoc 228 M params, 0.9 GB weights), global retrieval fails in haze, strict residual gate rejects blurred-but-correct fixes, needs height and heading (and tilt) hints, optimistic data (same map). Use: as an absolute-position corrector with an onboard prior (tracking mode) on GPU-class hardware; do not rely on global retrieval alone in low-contrast scenes or on CPU-only boards.
Known risks observed: (a) the first (oblique, body-fixed camera) dataset made the nadir assumption fail completely (north-up NCC 0.1-0.2); attitude had to be known to rectify (probe of 7 oblique frames with true attitude: 427-574 inliers, <0.5 m: results/s6/nidar_oblique/probe_7frames.txt, stress result "body-fixed 30-deg-oblique camera"); (b) hint yaw units (deg) and string-sorted frame names in the harness; (c) truth60.csv still carries the old -30 deg pitch; (d) T6 fallback dataset: not run (dataset unreachable, no open mirror attempted beyond the lead's note); (e) T7 SITL: not run by S6 (lead uses results/s6/nidar/S6-T1-20261023-s0/estimates.csv).

#### Commands for the lead (run ALONE, one at a time, from solutions/s6_jetson_composite with `source env/bin/activate; export OMP_NUM_THREADS=2`)
- T4 real-time replay with tracking: `python driver.py --run-id S6-T4-rt-<date>-s0 --mode realtime --cfg '{"tracking":true}'`
- Constrained (2 cores): `taskset -c 0,1 python driver.py --run-id S6-T4-c2-<date>-s0 --mode realtime --cfg '{"tracking":true}'` (add `systemd-run`/cgroup memory limit as desired)
- Clean latency (alone): `python driver.py --run-id S6-T1lat-<date>-s0 --stride 5`
- T5: `python t5_variants.py --run-id S6-T5-<date>-s0`
Extra per-frame stage timings are in extras.csv of each run.


### Setup account

### S6 "our composite" -- setup log

"Our composite" is NOT an existing project. It is a Jetson-oriented baseline assembled by us from permissive parts:
MegaLoc (retrieval) + FAISS tile index + XFeat/LighterGlue (matching) + planar PnP + consistency gate + tracking window.
All data below is synthetic NIDAR-like. The map used for retrieval is the SAME map the video was rendered from (optimistic appearance gap).

Host: Intel Xeon 2.10 GHz, 4 cores shared with other agents (load avg 7-9 most of the time), 15 GB RAM, no GPU, Python 3.12 (uv venv; system python is 3.13).

#### Commands that worked (from `solutions/s6_jetson_composite`)
```
export PIP_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/pipcache
uv venv --python 3.12 env && source env/bin/activate
uv pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu      # torch 2.14.1+cpu
uv pip install numpy opencv-python-headless faiss-cpu pycolmap onnx onnxruntime timm huggingface_hub pandas scipy kornia einops tqdm pillow safetensors
mkdir repo && cd repo
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/verlab/accelerated_features   # XFeat + LighterGlue weights live in the repo (weights/)
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/gmberton/MegaLoc
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/cvg/LightGlue && uv pip install -e LightGlue
uv pip uninstall opencv-python opencv-python-headless && uv pip install opencv-python-headless   # see failure 3
# MegaLoc weights (HF gberton/MegaLoc, model.safetensors, 0.87 GB) download on first load into repo/hf
cd .. && python driver.py --run-id S6-T1-20261023-s0 --stride 1
```
Pins: COMMIT.txt (MegaLoc 5fe0dd6, accelerated_features e92685f, LightGlue eb42fee), lock.txt (pip freeze).
Wall clock from clone to first working output: about 95 min (of which ~18 min MegaLoc index build under CPU contention, ~45 min tracking down the camera-geometry problem below). Failed steps: 6.

#### Failures and fixes
1. `torch.hub.load("gmberton/MegaLoc", ...)` -> `HTTP Error 400: Bad Request` (torch.hub fetches the GitHub zip/branch via api.github.com, not reachable through the proxy). Fix: `git clone` (works) and `torch.hub.load(<local clone>, "get_trained_model", source="local")`; this still uses MegaLoc's own hubconf and downloads weights from Hugging Face (reachable). Equivalent code path, different source.
2. `pip install lightglue` -> not on PyPI under that name. Fix: install from the git clone (cvg/LightGlue).
3. Installing LightGlue pulled `opencv-python` which shadows `opencv-python-headless` (twice, also after moving the clone). Fix: uninstall both, reinstall headless.
4. `uv pip install -e` pointed at a path I later moved (/tmp -> repo/); reinstalled from the final path.
5. TensorRT: `pip install tensorrt` -> sdist build aborts, "nvidia-smi command not found". `tensorrt-cu12==10.3.0` -> same build error (needs NVIDIA index + driver). `--no-deps tensorrt-cu12-libs` -> wheel extraction `No space left on device` (disk was shared and full). Three attempts, all failed; removed. No FP16 engine can be built without a GPU anyway.
6. Disk: uv cache reached 4 GB; purged (`uv cache clean`) after lead's notice. Env 1.6 GB, repo (incl. 0.87 GB weights) 1 GB.
7. Own mistakes: a `pkill -f driver.py` killed my own shell; deleting the symlink frame dir of a running job broke it (restarted).

#### Data defects found (reported to lead)
- Original frames were rendered with a body-fixed camera while the quad pitches -30 deg in cruise (truth60 pitch -0.52 rad) -> strongly oblique. Re-rendered by lead as gimbal nadir. NOTE: truth60.csv still contains the old pitch; our final runs use `att_source=hints` (roll=pitch=0) and ignore truth60.
- Harness hint yaw is in degrees (adapter converts). run_replay sorts file names as strings; our driver symlinks frames with zero-padded names.

## S7. Paper-only and special-purpose items (not ranked)

## S7 review: paper-only and special-purpose items

Compared on documentation, feasibility and relevance. NOT ranked against S1-S6; no shared accuracy numbers. All claimed numbers are author claims, unverified, unless stated. Date 2026-10-23. CPU: shared 4-core VM (lscpu model not exposed to agent), 2 threads, CPU only.

### 1. YFS90 terrain-weighted geolocalisation (documentation review only)
- Sources: repo https://github.com/YFS90/GNSS-Denied-UAV-Geolocalization (HEAD 968eaf8, 2024-11-28, single commit line, branch `main` only, no tags); paper Yao, Lan, Wang, Wan, Gao, Wei, "GNSS-denied geolocalization of UAVs using terrain-weighted constraint optimization", Int. J. Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation 135, 104277 (Dec 2024), doi 10.1016/j.jag.2024.104277. Full text was not retrievable here (ScienceDirect 403); the summary below uses the repo README and the published abstract, so it is high level.
- Plain-language method: the UAV image stream is (a) matched to publicly available satellite map tiles (the map is cut into chunks for memory management), (b) tracked frame to frame by visual odometry, and (c) a 2D-3D geo-registration step ("bidirectional homologous point search") lifts matched points to 3D "virtual control points" using public DEM terrain heights. A sliding-window optimisation then fuses matches and odometry, with each constraint weighted by terrain (so flat or featureless terrain is trusted less). Claimed to need no altimeter or IMU, no loop closure, no error accumulation, and to re-localise after a failure; also claimed to tolerate tilt, rotation, altitude change, season and light change.
- Code and weights: NONE. Verified: repo tree contains only README.md and Img/ (images, GIF, 20 result figures with bilibili/YouTube video links); `git ls-remote` shows only refs/heads/main; no tags or releases; README links no code, data or weights. The author's other public repo `Real-time-orthophoto` is a different paper (GPS-free orthophoto SLAM), not this system. We did not reimplement.
- Licence: no LICENSE file; all rights reserved by default, so reuse is not permitted. Paper is journal-published (check ScienceDirect access terms).
- Claimed data/results (unverified): 20 scenarios (plains, hills, urban, rural, multiple viewpoints, seasons, thermal infrared night); abstract claims mean absolute error under 7 m; README claims accuracy "comparable to GPS". No per-scenario table seen by us.
- Feasibility on Jetson Orin class: unknown; no runtime reported in the material we could read, and without code it cannot be tested; a reimplementation would be a multi-month project (VO + DEM registration + windowed optimisation).
- Relevance to NIDAR (200 m nadir, 1280x800 grey, 0.18 m/px): conceptually highly relevant (satellite matching plus VO plus no IMU need, absolute fixes with no drift), and DEM terrain weighting matters little over the flat Pune site. Currently unusable: nothing to run.
- Documentation rubric 0-3: install steps 0 (no code); config explained 0; results reproducible 0 (videos only); algorithm described 1 (README is a marketing summary; detail lives in the paywalled paper).

### 2. Bearing-UAV (CVPR 2026)
- Sources: paper "Beyond Matching to Tiles: Bridging Unaligned Aerial and Satellite Views for Vision-Only UAV Navigation", Liu et al., arXiv 2603.22153 (CVPR 2026); code https://github.com/liukejia121/bearinguav (HEAD d16e558, 2026-05-01); weights https://huggingface.co/HaoyZhou/bearinguav (Bearing_UAV.zip, 131 MB, ungated, no HF licence tag); dataset Bearing-UAV-90K on HF (single 6.3 GB zip, NOT downloaded; we read only the 225-row mini metadata and 3 sample blocks via HTTP range to learn the input format).
- Plain-language method: it is not a matcher. A VGG-16 backbone (frozen, ImageNet) plus a non-local/clustering head turns each of five 256x256 images into a descriptor: four satellite tiles forming a 2x2 block and one UAV patch. A relative-coordinate encoder, patch-similarity prior and cross-attention fuse them, and two regression heads output the UAV position inside the block and heading as (cos, sin). A "Bearing-Naver" scheme steps along waypoints using it. Needs a known starting block (prior), no map-wide search.
- Code/weights: both released. Licence Apache-2.0 (code); dataset/weights licence not stated. Weights run on CPU (about 133 ms per step in the paper on GPU; here median 4.4 s per sample on a loaded shared 4-core CPU at 2 threads).
- Claimed results (unverified, author claims, own Google-Earth-3D-rendered data): mean localisation error 8.61 m (7.48 m with weather aug), mean heading error 12.90 deg, Recall@1 83.2%, LSR@15 89.4%, HSR@15 77.2%; waypoint navigation success only about 50% (SR@20), navigation error 275 m. Model about 68 MB, 10.5 GFLOPs at 256x256.
- Our run (labelled SYNTHETIC NIDAR-like, out of distribution; results/s7/bearing/S7-B-20261023-s0/): driver `solutions/s7_paper_only/bearing_driver.py`. Four 64 m tiles cut from the Esri reference map (same map the video was rendered from, so optimistic) around an oracle block centre placed at truth plus a seeded random offset (+-0.9 units = +-29 m); UAV patch = central 64 m (356 px) crop of our frame resized to 256. 153 frames (1 Hz subset, seed 0). Metrics via harness/metrics.py summarize(): median position error 28.2 m, p95 48.8 m, RMSE 30.2 m, max 59.7 m, 100% "fix" rate (the model always answers). Trivial baseline "predict block centre" (the oracle prior itself): median 23.1 m, mean 22.2 m. So the model is NOT better than the prior here. Heading: median error 93.6 deg, mean 96.2 deg, i.e. chance level (random is about 90 deg); heading convention is assumed (see caveats), and the nadir 64 m crop of a straight-down 1280x800 image does not look like the paper's Google-Earth 3D rendered views.
- Sanity check of the code path (results/s7/sanity/dataset_samples.json): on 3 samples from the paper's own mini dataset the released weights give 3.9, 1.5, 1.6 m and 2.4, 11.2, 2.7 deg errors (3 samples only; may be training data; shows weights and driver load correctly).
- Caveats: tile geometry assumed contiguous 64 m tiles at p1..p4 = (-1,-1),(-1,+1),(+1,-1),(+1,+1) in (x east, y south) units of 32 m; the sample tiles looked non-contiguous so the real layout may differ; heading frame (image-up = heading) assumed; scale 0.25 m/px per 256 px assumed from README/config; the 64 m footprint is much narrower than our true 230x144 m footprint; sat tiles from different imagery source than training (Google Earth). The negative result therefore means "no evidence of use out of the box", not "the method cannot work".
- Feasibility on Jetson Orin class: yes, small VGG-16 style network (68 MB, 10.5 GFLOPs), likely tens of ms on Orin GPU; but needs retraining for our camera and a known-start block.
- Relevance to NIDAR: low-to-medium; designed for oblique/3D-rendered urban views with a known starting block, only about 50% waypoint success in its own paper, regression gives no confidence/inlier check; fine-tuning on NIDAR-like data would be needed (not done: instructed not to train).
- Documentation rubric 0-3: install steps 1 (README lists CUDA 11.8 / Python 3.9 pins; Python 3.13 and torch 2.1.2 not installable, we used py3.11 CPU torch 2.1.2; imgaug/albumentations imported at module load although unused for inference; ImageNet VGG16 weights silently downloaded at model build, 528 MB); config explained 2 (JSON config shipped with weights); results reproducible 1 (test script and weights exist but need the 6.3 GB zip and GPU-style paths, no inference-on-your-own-images example); algorithm described 2 (paper plus architecture tree; heading/tile conventions undocumented).
- Setup effort: about 45 min wall clock, 4 failed steps: (1) gh API access to repo denied (used add_repo then git clone), (2) pip torch 2.1.2 not available for Python 3.13 (used 3.11 venv), (3) two installs failed with "No space left on device" (shared disk dipped to 185 MB free; retried after space returned), (4) imgaug missing (stubbed). Env 1.4 GB, weights 262 MB (git-ignored).

### 3. STHN thermal homography
- Sources: repo https://github.com/arplaboratory/STHN (HEAD 0b44a84, 2026-05-16); paper Xiao, Zhang, Tortei, Loianno, IEEE RA-L 9(10) 2024, arXiv 2405.20470 (v3 Sep 2025); weights on HF: xjh19972/STHN (one_stage 6.5 MB, two_stages 12.3 MB safetensors) and xjh19972/STHN-one-stage; dataset (122 GB) NOT downloaded, as instructed.
- Plain-language method: given a thermal image from straight-down UAV camera and a larger satellite crop around the last known position, a CNN predicts how the four corners of the thermal image move to land on the satellite image (homography via DLT). Coarse stage: both images resized to 256 px, iterative correlation-based updates (6 iterations). Optional fine stage: crop the satellite image around the coarse result and refine. A pix2pix-style "thermal generative module" synthesises fake thermal images from satellite tiles to enlarge training data. The location is the image centre mapped into the satellite frame. Works within a 512 m search radius of the last known position, even with the thermal image only 11% the satellite size.
- Code/weights: both released. Licence MIT (code, LICENSE file "Copyright 2024 ARPL"); data/weights licence not stated. Demo script STHN_demo.py runs on one sample pair (needs conda env.yml, torch, kornia).
- Claimed results (unverified): MACE 12.70 m (two-stage, 512 m offset, 0% failures), 16.42 m (one-stage), localisation error 12.12 m at 63.9 ms on an RTX 2080 Ti; keypoint baselines fail 83-99.7%.
- Run: not run. Not applicable: models are trained for 8-bit thermal (Boson, about 1 m/px, night) and our payload is visible grayscale at 0.18 m/px, so a thermal-trained model would be out of domain; running it would not produce meaningful evidence. Weights existence verified by the HF listing only.
- Feasibility on Jetson Orin class: yes; tiny models (6.5-12 MB) and paper reports 64 ms on a desktop GPU.
- Relevance to NIDAR: not applicable to the visible payload; useful only if a thermal camera is ever added (night operation). The homography-regression idea (bounded search around last position, no dense tile search) is conceptually transferable, but would need retraining on visible-to-satellite pairs.
- Documentation rubric 0-3: install 2 (env.yml plus demo that pulls weights automatically); config explained 2 (scripts per setting, HF config.json); results reproducible 2 (weights, 122 GB data and train/eval scripts; slurm-oriented); algorithm described 3 (paper, README architecture notes, code links).

### 3.8 Weighted ranking and sensitivity

Scores are min-max scaled to 0-10 across the solutions that ran each test; a solution that could not run a test gets 0 for it and is shown as *not run*. Weights are the owner's (30/20/20/15/15).

- **Accuracy** = mean of median error (accepted fixes), p95 error and recall@50 m, on the common 153 frames.
- **Robustness** = mean of accepted-fix precision@100 m, recall@100 m inside blur/haze windows, and the worst terrain-class recall@50 m. (The failure-injection tests differ between solutions, so the shared weather windows are the common basis.)
- **Real-time and edge fit** = mean of constrained-replay p50 latency, real-time processed-frame share and peak memory. CPU only; no Jetson number exists.
- **SITL outcome** = mean of mission-completion share and (log10) maximum EKF error over SIM-2 to SIM-7, 3 seeds each.
- **Integration, documentation and licence** = mean of setup effort (minutes + 10 per failed step), documentation rubric, licence class (permissive 10, copyleft 5, non-commercial 3, none declared 1) and maturity (a judgement from the repository facts, 0-10).

## 4. SITL results (ArduCopter 4.5.7, scenarios SIM-0 to SIM-7, 3 seeds)

**Method.** ArduCopter 4.5.7 SITL at 8x speed. Take-off to 200 m, then the A→B→C→D mission in GUIDED at 12 m/s. A second GPS (`GPS_TYPE2 = 14`, MAVLink) receives `GPS_INPUT` messages from `harness/sitl_bridge.py` (accepted fixes only; velocity, altitude and accuracy-of-speed fields ignored; horizontal accuracy from the solution's confidence; each fix projected forward to the send time with the EKF velocity). EKF3 is set to position-only GPS (`EK3_SRC1_POSXY=3`, `VELXY=0`, `POSZ=1` baro), `EK3_GPS_CHECK=0`. The real GPS is cut with `SIM_GPS_DISABLE=1` at mission time t = 60 s (t = 0 in SIM-6) and the second GPS becomes primary. A run **fails** when the EKF raises a failsafe that ends the mission (LAND) or the vehicle leaves the planned corridor by more than 200 m. Final parameter files, bridge logs, EKF-vs-truth traces and dataflash logs (seed 0, git-ignored) are in `results/<row>/sitl/<scenario>-s<seed>/`.

| ID | Scenario |
|---|---|
| SIM-0 | GPS stays on; solution only logged (fixes not sent) |
| SIM-1 | GPS cut at 60 s, no vision: dead-reckoning control |
| SIM-2 | GPS cut at 60 s, solution feeds `GPS_INPUT` (main test) |
| SIM-3 | as SIM-2, solution output dropped in 20 s windows (80-100 s and 125-145 s) |
| SIM-4a/4b | as SIM-2 with 200 ms / 500 ms added latency |
| SIM-5 | as SIM-2 with 5 % of fixes moved by 100-300 m |
| SIM-6 | GPS cut at the start of cruise (cold start; take-off cut not possible, see deviations) |
| SIM-7 | full mission with GPS cut at 60 s, then return-to-launch with no vision on the way back (the recorded video ends at D) |

Rows other than S1-S6: a **control** (ground truth plus 5 m noise as fixes) shows what the EKF achieves with ideal fixes; "S2 VIO-only" is the S2 odometry track without map fixes; "S3 + compass de-rotation" is our extension. These rows are not ranked.

## 5. Findings and next steps

### Adopt
- **Retrieve → match → PnP → gate → track (S6 structure).** Evidence: S6-T1 (764 frames, 92.8 % fixed, 0.41 m median, 100 % precision), S6-T4 with tracking (95.3 % fixed, bridges the blur/haze gaps), SITL SIM-2/4/6/7 completed in all seeds. Retrieval quality is the lever: MegaLoc recall@1 84.3 % against 39.9 % for DINOv2-small CLS+mean-patch (S6-T2), and XFeat+LighterGlue loses only 8 points of fix rate against SuperPoint+LightGlue while running 4x faster (S6-T3).
- **A consistency gate with barometer and compass hints.** S1 and S6 produced no wrong fix above 8 m (S1) or none over 100 m (S6); S3 without any gate accepted 7 wrong fixes of 52 (precision@100 m 86.5 %), and S2's consensus step accepted 84 fixes of which 7 % were right (the wrong fixes agreed with each other).
- **Orienting the frame to the map with the compass.** De-rotating S3's frames raised its fix rate from 34 % to 56 % with no other change.

### Drop or do not rely on
- **S2 as tested.** Retrieval near chance (4.6 % recall@100 m) with our 50-minute CPU-trained CAEVL; fused RMSE 798 m against 5 m for the VIO alone. Fusion does help a drifting VIO if fixes are good (synthetic sanity test: 50-67 % lower RMSE with 20-40 % good fixes) but never helped here, so the author's 36 % claim is **not reproduced and not refuted** (different encoder, VIO, data).
- **S3 as a standalone localiser** (no rotation handling, no gate, 6-14 s per step on CPU).
- **S1 with pretrained weights.** The author's fine-tuned DINOv2 is not published; with DINOv2-base the true tile ranks 11-212 of 1,225 under blur and haze, and fixes exist only for the first 44 s.
- **S4** cannot be judged: the 6.9 GB image, PX4/Gazebo build, GPU and X11 requirements did not fit here. Its matcher needs a prior position and heading, so it cannot localise from a cold start, and ArduPilot support is marked unmaintained.

### Methodological findings
- **The video must be nadir.** Our first render used a body-fixed camera on a quadcopter that pitches −30° in cruise: every solution failed or needed rectification (S5 106.8 m median error without rectification; S6's nadir assumption failed completely). Any real NIDAR payload needs a gimbal or an attitude-aware rectification stage; S5's and S6's rectification extensions recover it only with accurate attitude.
- **Same-map imagery inflates accuracy.** Median errors of 0.07-0.4 m for S3 and S6 are a property of the test, not of the methods.
- **The EKF side matters as much as the vision side.** With a position-only second GPS, the EKF3 failsafe lands the vehicle about 68 s into the flight with no vision (SIM-1) and within about 8 s of the start of a 20 s fix drop-out (SIM-3 lands at about 88 s, even for ideal 5 m-noise fixes). 5 % outliers of 100-300 m (SIM-5) cost S5 and S6 two thirds of their missions: the fix quality gate needs to run on the autopilot side as well.
- **Latency.** On this CPU the steps cost 0.06 s (S2), 0.9 s (S6), 3-16 s (S5), 5.6 s (S3), 8.8 s (S1). Only S2 (poor fixes) and S6 (partly) approach a 5 Hz stream; the others need a GPU or a much lighter model before they can run at the frame rate.

### Next three tests (in order)
1. **S6 on real NIDAR video with a reference map of a different date**, with the thresholds frozen beforehand and a held-out flight. This removes the three optimism sources (same-map imagery, tuning on the test frames, noise-free hints).
2. **S6 on a Jetson Orin with TensorRT FP16**, measuring the whole pipeline (MegaLoc, XFeat, LighterGlue, PnP) at 5 Hz and its power mode; LighterGlue's ONNX export failed here and must be solved first.
3. **Closed-loop SITL (Gazebo-rendered camera) with a velocity/odometry aid in the EKF**, comparing S6 and S5 on feature-poor terrain (forest, water, fields) and with an injected fix outage and outliers, to fix the position-only EKF limits seen in SIM-3 and SIM-5.

## Appendices

### A. Reproduction commands
```
# data (synthetic NIDAR-like), from the repository root gpsdenied-eval/
python tools/fetch_esri_map.py --lat 18.5204 --lon 73.8567 --half_m 900 --z 19 --out data/nidar/map_esri_z19.png
python tools/sitl_mission.py --out data/nidar/flight_sitl            # ArduCopter SITL A->B->C->D at 200 m AGL
python tools/render_video.py --flight data/nidar/flight_sitl --map data/nidar/map_esri_z19.png --out data/nidar --stabilised
# harness tests
cd harness && python -m pytest test_harness.py
# SITL scenarios for one solution (3 seeds x 9 scenario rows)
python harness/run_sitl_all.py --solution s6 --estimates results/s6/nidar/S6-T1-<date>-s0/estimates.csv
# serial latency / real-time / constrained runs
bash report/serial_latency.sh
# report
python harness/collect.py --runs report/runs.json --out report/metrics_master.json
python harness/terrain.py --runs report/runs.json --out report/terrain.json --fig report/figures/terrain_breakdown.png
python harness/plots.py --runs report/runs.json --out report/figures
python harness/arch_svg.py report/arch
python harness/report_build.py
```
Per-solution replay commands are in each `SETUP.md` / `ANALYSIS.md`.
